title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: This policy states how a loss, occurrence, accident, or other event becomes a Northline Assurance claim. It tells staff what information must be captured at first notice, who is allowed to report, how fast the Company must acknowledge the report, and what happens when notice is late, incomplete, duplicated, or delivered by someone other than the named insured.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A claim file is the official record of the Company's handling. The first notice of loss is the moment that record begins. Errors at intake — a wrong date of loss, a missed mortgagee, an unlogged attorney letter, a second file opened for the same event — travel through coverage, reserves, and payment. This policy exists so those errors are caught at the door.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Where a statute, regulation, or the insurance contract sets a stricter rule than this document, the stricter rule controls. State addenda issued by Compliance override the timelines in Section 8 for the states they name. This document is an operating policy for Northline staff. It is not a coverage grant and it does not amend any policy issued to a customer.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Every person who can open, receive, or redirect a claim must follow this policy. That includes the 24-hour First Notice Desk, branch claim associates, staff field adjusters, independent adjusters appointed by Northline, third-party administrators handling Northline paper, and any underwriter or agent who is handed a loss notice by a customer. Agents may receive notice. They may not decide coverage, set a reserve, or tell a customer a claim will be paid.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A person must submit a claim, or the Company must open a file on its own initiative, when any of the following is true:
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text:
- An insured, additional insured, loss payee, mortgagee, or other person claiming under a Northline policy reports bodily injury, property damage, loss of use, or a circumstance that may later produce either.
- A third party asserts that a Northline insured caused injury or damage, even if the insured has not yet called.
- The Company receives a summons, complaint, attorney representation letter, department-of-insurance inquiry, or medical-provider lien that identifies a Northline policy or insured.
- A Northline policyholder reports a weather event, theft, fire, water loss, collision, or other incident and asks whether it is covered. Asking "is this covered?" is notice. Staff open a file and then answer the coverage question under CLM-002. They do not answer coverage on the phone with no file.
- Reinsurance, a fronting partner, or a managing general agent forwards a loss that attaches to a Northline contract.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Staff do not open a claim file for a pure billing dispute, a request for a policy change, or a coverage question about a hypothetical future event. Those go to service or underwriting. If the caller then describes an event that has already happened, the call becomes a claim and the file is opened before the call ends.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: The intake rules in this policy are the same across lines. What changes is the data that must be collected and the desk the file is routed to. Personal auto files route to the Auto Liability or Auto Physical Damage queue based on whether injury or only vehicle damage is reported. Homeowners and commercial property route to Property. Commercial general liability routes to Casualty. A single event that touches more than one policy — a house fire that also destroys a scheduled boat and injures a guest — produces one event record and as many claim files as there are policies, linked by the event number. Staff never force two policies into one claim number.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Acknowledgment.** A written or electronic confirmation that Northline has received the notice, has opened a claim, and has given the claimant the claim number, the name of a contact, and a description of what the Company still needs.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Claimant.** Any person or organization seeking payment under a Northline policy or alleging injury or damage caused by a Northline insured. The insured and a third party can both be claimants on the same event.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Date of loss.** The date the injury, damage, or loss occurred. For a continuing condition, such as a slow leak, the date of loss is the date the insured first knew or, with reasonable attention, should have known of the damage, unless the policy defines the date differently. Staff record both the date damage began and the date it was discovered when those dates differ, and they do not pick one silently.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Event number.** The identifier for the real-world incident. One event may have several claim numbers.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **First notice of loss (FNOL).** The earliest report to Northline, or to an agent the policy designates as a person to whom notice may be given, that a loss or occurrence has happened.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Late notice.** Notice received after the time required by the policy or, where the policy is silent, after the time a reasonably diligent person would have reported given the facts. Late notice is a coverage issue under CLM-002. It is not a reason to refuse to open a file.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Named insured.** The person or organization listed on the declarations. Additional insureds, loss payees, and mortgagees have their own reporting rights as described in Section 5.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Northline Claim File (NCF).** The system of record. A note in email, a text message, or an adjuster's notebook is not the claim file until it is entered in NCF.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Proof of loss.** The signed statement of the amount and cause of loss that some property policies require as a condition. A first notice is not a proof of loss. Staff must not treat the intake conversation as if the insured had already sworn to the amount claimed.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Reporter.** The person who actually contacts Northline. The reporter may or may not be the claimant.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text:
1. **Open the file first.** If the report describes an event that may involve a Northline policy, staff open the claim before they debate whether it will be paid. A refusal to open a file is not a coverage decision, and it leaves the Company with no record of what it was told.
2. **The customer is told the truth about what has and has not been decided.** Intake staff may say "we have opened a claim and an adjuster will review coverage." They may not say "you are covered," "this will be denied," or "we always pay this."
3. **Notice to an appointed agent is notice to the Company** when the policy or agency agreement says so. The clock for acknowledgment runs from the day the agent received the notice, not from the day the agent remembered to forward it. Agents must forward notice the same business day.
4. **One event, linked files.** Duplicate claim numbers for the same policy and the same event are a defect. Staff search before they create.
5. **The person who reports does not have to use any particular words.** "I think my pipe burst," "someone hit my car and left," and "my tenant is being sued" are all notice if they identify an event and a possible Northline policy.
6. **Vulnerable claimants are not processed on the standard script alone.** A report involving a fatality, a hospitalized minor, a person who does not speak the language of the call, or a person who says they cannot safely return to the property is flagged at intake and assigned the same day. See Section 6.4.
7. **Nothing in this policy limits a duty the Company owes under unfair-claims-settlement law.** When this manual and that law diverge, staff follow the law and record the variance.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: 5.1 Insureds and people acting for them
section: 5.1 Insureds and people acting for them
text: The named insured, a spouse or resident relative who is an insured under the policy, an officer or authorized employee of a commercial named insured, and a person holding a written power of attorney may submit a claim and may receive claim information. Staff verify identity before they discuss policy limits, prior claims, or payment status. Verification is the caller's full name, the policy number or insured address, and one additional item that is not public: the last four digits of the tax identifier on the billing account, a vehicle identification number, or a recent billing amount. Staff do not ask for a full Social Security number on an unsecured phone call.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: 5.1 Insureds and people acting for them
section: 5.1 Insureds and people acting for them
text: A household member who is not an insured may report an event. Staff open the file. They do not release coverage details or payment information to that person until an insured authorizes it in writing or the policy gives that person rights of their own.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: 5.2 Additional insureds, mortgagees, and loss payees
section: 5.2 Additional insureds, mortgagees, and loss payees
text: An additional insured may report a claim seeking defense or indemnity for a suit against them. A mortgagee or loss payee may report damage to property in which they have a recorded interest, even if the named insured has not called and even if the named insured disagrees. When a mortgagee reports and the named insured does not, staff still notify the named insured in writing within two business days that a claim has been opened on the property. Payment rules for dual payees are in CLM-005. Intake must capture the mortgagee name, loan number if known, and mailing address so the loss payee is not discovered for the first time at payment.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A person who says a Northline insured injured them or damaged their property may report the claim. Staff open a liability file. They do not give the third party the insured's home telephone number, policy limit, or a coverage opinion at intake. They do give the claim number, a description of the next step, and a request for the third party's own damage information. If the third party is represented by a lawyer, all later contact goes to the lawyer once representation is confirmed. See Section 6.3.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Captive agents and independent agents appointed by Northline must accept notice and must enter it in NCF, or must send the completed NAC-CLM-100 to the First Notice Desk, on the business day they receive it. An agent who tells a customer "I'll let claims know" has received notice for the Company. An agent may help the customer describe the loss. An agent may not estimate the settlement, advise the customer to wait and see if the damage gets worse before reporting, or discourage a report because the customer's premium might rise. Any such statement is reported to Agency Management the same day.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A lawyer, public adjuster, or other representative may submit a claim only with an authorization signed by the person they represent, or with a letter of representation that identifies the client and the event. Form NAC-CLM-108 is preferred. A representation letter on firm letterhead is acceptable if it names the client, the date of loss, and the property or injury. Until that writing is in the file, staff may take the factual report from the representative so the file can be opened, and they may not discuss settlement authority or issue payment to the representative.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Northline does not require a customer to hire a public adjuster or a lawyer, and staff do not suggest one. Northline also does not refuse to speak with a properly authorized representative. Once authorization is on file, copies of claims correspondence go to the representative and to the customer unless the customer has directed in writing that correspondence go only to the representative.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A parent or legal guardian may report a claim for a minor child. Payment to a minor is governed by CLM-005 and often requires a court-approved guardian or a restricted account. Intake records the minor's age and the reporter's relationship. Staff do not ask a minor to give a recorded statement at intake.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: If the named insured has died, the person reporting must identify themselves and their relationship. Staff open the file and request letters of appointment for the estate before any payment or any recorded statement about the merits. Emergency board-up and make-safe work may still be authorized so the property does not deteriorate. That authorization is not an admission that the estate's claim will be paid.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Northline accepts first notice by:
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss
CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Social-media messages, text messages to an employee's personal phone, and voicemail left on a closed branch line are not monitored claim channels. If an employee happens to receive one and it describes a loss, the employee forwards it to the First Notice Desk the same day and does not handle it from a personal device. The Company does not promise a response time on unmonitored channels, and marketing does not publish them as claim contacts.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A notice is complete enough to open when staff have, or have documented why they do not yet have, the following:
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text:
| Item | Why it is required |
| --- | --- |
| Reporter name, phone, email, and relationship to the insured | So the Company can call back and know whom it may speak with |
| Named insured and policy number, or enough to search: name plus address, vehicle, or business | So the file attaches to a contract |
| Date and time of loss, and the date the insured discovered it if different | Coverage, deductibles, and late-notice analysis all depend on it |
| Location of the loss | Jurisdiction, catastrophe coding, and inspection assignment |
| Short description of what happened and what is damaged or who is hurt | Routing, reserve, and injury flag |
| Whether police, fire, or medical care was involved, and any report number | Liability and fraud indicators |
| For property: whether the property is habitable and whether a mortgage exists | Emergency living expense and loss-payee notice |
| For auto: year, make, model, plate or VIN, other driver if known, and whether anyone was injured or taken from the scene | Coverage part and injury desk |
| For liability: name of the claimant if known, and whether a lawsuit or lawyer letter has arrived | Litigation hold and counsel assignment |
| Preferred language | So later contact is not conducted in a language the person does not understand |
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: If the caller cannot supply a policy number, staff search NCF and the policy administration system by name, address, and vehicle. If no policy is found, staff still record the report as an unmatched notice, give the reporter a reference number, and tell them the search result. Unmatched notices are worked by the desk supervisor within one business day. They are not deleted because the first search failed.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Staff do not require, at intake, a contractor estimate, a recorded statement, medical records, or a signed proof of loss. Asking for those items is part of investigation under CLM-003. Requiring them before a claim number exists delays acknowledgment and is not permitted.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Any employee who receives a summons, complaint, or letter of representation delivers it to the Litigation Intake queue the day it is received, by scan if the original is paper. The original paper is sent the same day by internal courier or overnight mail. Litigation Intake opens or links the claim, places a litigation hold on the file so routine destruction stops, and refers the suit to assigned defense counsel under the panel rules. A lawsuit is not held at a branch for the producer to "look into it." The time to answer a complaint runs from service, not from the day Claims happens to see the paper.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: The First Notice Desk flags and warm-transfers, or assigns within two hours, any report that includes:
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss
CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Make-safe authority for temporary repairs, board-up, and water mitigation may be given at intake up to the associate limit in CLM-004 so the loss does not get worse. That spend is an expense or an indemnity payment according to the coverage part, and it is coded as incurred before the coverage decision is final when waiting would increase the damage. The file note must say that the spend was to protect the property and is subject to the later coverage decision.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Before creating a claim, staff search NCF for the policy number and the date of loss, plus or minus three days, and for the location address. If a file exists for the same policy and the same event, the new information is added to that file. A second file is opened only when a second policy, a second claimant who needs a separate liability evaluation, or a second coverage part that the system cannot hold on the first file requires it. The files are cross-linked the same day.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A weather event that affects many insureds is not a reason to skip the search. Catastrophe coding under CLM-010 is applied after the duplicate check, not instead of it.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: The person who opens the file enters the minimum data set, the channel, the date and time notice reached Northline or its agent, and a factual narrative in the reporter's words. The narrative is not rewritten into coverage language. "Caller states the kitchen ceiling fell in after two days of heavy rain and they first saw staining last night" is acceptable. "Covered windstorm; pay the roof" is not. Opinions about fault, fraud, or coverage may be entered only in the designated analysis fields, separated from the factual narrative, and only by someone whose job includes that analysis.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: The opener sets the initial line of business, the injury flag if any person may be hurt, the catastrophe code if Claims Management has opened a CAT event, and the diary for first contact. The opener does not set a coverage indicator to "covered."
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Every open indemnity file carries a reserve before the end of the business day it is opened, using the intake reserve schedule published by Finance and Claims. A file with a zero indemnity reserve overnight is an exception that requires a supervisor note explaining why no payment is possible, for example a report-only notice on a liability policy where no claimant has been identified and no injury is alleged. Expense reserves are posted when the file is assigned to a field adjuster or an expert. Reserve method is governed by CLM-004. Intake staff do not guess a high number "to be safe" and they do not leave the reserve at one dollar.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Standard files are assigned by the routing rules in NCF: geography, line of business, license where a state requires a licensed adjuster, current workload, and language. A file is not assigned to the employee who sold the policy. Files in which the claimant is a Northline employee, an agent's household, or a relative of the assigned adjuster are reassigned by a supervisor to a person with no personal connection, and the relationship is noted.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: The assigned adjuster owns the file until it is transferred or closed. Ownership includes first contact, the coverage screen, the reserve, and the customer updates required in Section 8. A transfer requires a note that says what has been done, what is owed next, and the date of the last customer contact. Silent transfers are a handling defect.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Times in this section are Company standards. If the state unfair-claims law or the policy wording requires a faster acknowledgment, a faster decision, or a specific content in the letter, the state addendum controls. The First Notice Desk keeps the addendum dates in NCF so staff do not rely on memory.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text:
| Step | Standard | Clock starts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open the claim and give a claim number by phone or portal | During the contact, if the report is by phone or portal | When the report is received |
| Acknowledge in writing (letter or the customer's chosen electronic method) | 1 business day from receipt of notice; same day if the state addendum says so | When notice reached the Company or its appointed agent |
| First outbound contact by the assigned adjuster | 1 business day after assignment | Assignment |
| If no one answers, second and third attempts on different days and at different times, plus a written attempt | Within 5 business days of assignment | Assignment |
| Tell the claimant what documents are still needed, in writing | With the acknowledgment, and again when the list changes | Receipt of notice |
| Status update if the file remains open and no other letter has gone out | Every 15 business days | Last substantive communication |
| Request a signed proof of loss, if the policy requires one and the facts justify the request | Not at intake by default; only after the adjuster has enough facts to tell the insured what to complete | Adjuster's documented decision |
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A voicemail that does not say who called, the claim number, and a direct return number does not count as an attempt. A letter sent to an address the file shows is vacant does not count as notice to the insured. Staff use the last confirmed contact and record returned mail the day it comes back.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Form NAC-CLM-101, or the portal message that mirrors it, includes:
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss
CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: The acknowledgment does not quote a settlement amount, does not waive any policy condition, and does not use the phrase "this claim is not covered" unless a denial has been approved under CLM-006.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Staff accept the report whenever it arrives. They record when the event happened, when the insured learned of it, when notice reached the Company, and the reason given for any delay. They do not lecture the caller and they do not refuse the claim number. Whether late notice defeats coverage is decided under CLM-002 after the adjuster looks at prejudice to the Company's investigation. A file note that says only "late, deny" is not an analysis and will be returned by quality review.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Examples that still require a file and a real analysis:
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text:
- A homeowner reports hail six months after a storm because they noticed leaks only when they sold the house.
- A business reports a slip and fall four months after the date on a lawyer's letter, and says it never received an earlier complaint.
- An insured rear-ended another car, exchanged information, and called three weeks later after the other driver asked for payment.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: In each case the file is opened the day of the call. The coverage question is sequential, not a reason to turn the caller away.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: If the report lacks a piece of the minimum data set, staff open the file with what they have, send the acknowledgment describing the gap, and diary a follow-up in three business days. They do not hold the notice in an email inbox until the customer sends everything. An inbox is not a claim file. Supervisors review any notice email older than one business day that has not been converted to a claim or to a documented non-claim.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: 9. Proof of loss and other formal statements
section: 9. Proof of loss and other formal statements
text: Some property policies require a signed and sworn proof of loss within a stated number of days after the Company requests it. Northline requests a proof of loss when the amount claimed is disputed, when the insured is represented by a public adjuster and the figures conflict with the adjuster's measurement, when fraud indicators are present and SIU has concurred, or when the policy condition will be relied on. Northline does not send a proof of loss form on every kitchen-sink leak as a ritual.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: 9. Proof of loss and other formal statements
section: 9. Proof of loss and other formal statements
text: When a proof is requested, the letter states the contractual deadline, encloses or links form NAC-CLM-104, and identifies the documents that will help the insured complete it. The Company may extend the deadline in writing. An adjuster who needs more time to inspect must not use the proof deadline as a substitute for scheduling the inspection. If the insured submits a timely proof that is incomplete, staff say what is missing within ten business days and allow a reasonable time to cure. A denial based solely on the proof-of-loss condition requires supervisor approval under CLM-006 and a file that shows prejudice or an express policy failure that the jurisdiction enforces.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: 9. Proof of loss and other formal statements
section: 9. Proof of loss and other formal statements
text: Examinations under oath, medical examinations, and recorded statements are investigation tools under CLM-003. They are not part of first notice and they are not demanded in the acknowledgment letter by default.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A duplicate is a second claim number for the same policy, same event, and same coverage part. The surviving file is the one with the earlier notice date unless payments have already been issued on the later file, in which case the file that holds the payments survives and the other file's documents are moved to it. The discarded number is closed with a cross-reference, not deleted, so the old number still resolves in search. Payments are never "moved" by reissuing them to a new number without a reconciliation note from Claim Accounting.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A closed file is reopened when new damage from the same event is reported, a payment bounces, a lawsuit is served, or Recovery finds a subrogation opportunity that was not pursued. The adjuster states why the file was reopened and resets the reserve. A reopen within thirty days of closure is reviewed by a supervisor to see whether the closure was premature. Reopen for a new event, even at the same address, is a new claim.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A supplemental request on an open or recently closed property file — a contractor finds additional wet drywall after demolition — is handled on the original claim if it is the same cause of loss and the same occurrence. Staff inspect or document why a second inspection is unnecessary, update the estimate, and do not require the insured to "start over" with a new proof package if the original package plus the supplement is enough to decide.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: 11. What intake staff must not do
section: 11. What intake staff must not do
text:
- They must not deny a claim, in whole or in part, on the phone. Denials follow CLM-006.
- They must not promise a payment date or an amount.
- They must not tell an insured to repair everything and "send the bills" on a loss that has not been inspected, except for reasonable make-safe work described in Section 6.4.
- They must not discourage a report, suggest that a small claim be paid out of pocket to "protect the policy," or advise a customer on how the claim might affect renewal. Underwriting decides renewal. Claims decides the loss.
- They must not give legal advice. They may read a policy condition aloud and say that coverage has not yet been determined.
- They must not discuss one claimant's medical condition or settlement with another claimant.
- They must not alter a recorded fact because a later speaker prefers a different date of loss. Both statements stay in the file, attributed to the speaker, with the time they were made.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Staff use plain language. They say "we have not finished the coverage review" rather than "liability is undetermined pending completion of the investigation into the loss facts as they pertain to the insuring agreement." They use the customer's preferred language when the language line or a bilingual adjuster is available. A child does not serve as the interpreter for a parent's recorded statement or for a coverage explanation. A family member may help schedule a call. The substantive explanation is given through a qualified interpreter, and the use of the interpreter is noted.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Call recording follows the notice played at the start of the line. Staff do not record a call on a personal phone. After a lawyer has appeared, staff do not call the represented person directly except to confirm a fact the lawyer has authorized in writing, such as a property-access appointment the insured personally will attend.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Every outbound letter that asks the customer to do something states a date by which it would help, the consequence if the policy makes one, and a direct way to ask questions. Letters that exist only to "document the file" and that a reasonable customer would not understand are rewritten.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: When Claims Management declares a catastrophe event under CLM-010, the First Notice Desk switches to the CAT script for the affected geography and peril. The minimum data set still applies. The differences are: a CAT code is attached at opening, aerial or desk adjustment may replace an immediate site visit, acknowledgment times in the CAT bulletin may be extended only to the extent state law allows, and make-safe authority is confirmed in the bulletin so intake does not wait for a field assignment to authorize tarping. A CAT declaration never authorizes staff to skip duplicate searches or to tell customers that all storm claims will be paid.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: The claim file contains the notice, the acknowledgment, the recording or portal transcript if one exists, all later submissions, and a log of attempts to reach the customer. Personal information is collected only for handling the claim. Staff do not copy driver's-license images into email signatures or store claim photos on a personal cloud account. Retention is governed by CLM-009's companion records standard and by the Records Schedule maintained by Compliance: claim files are kept for the period required by the state with the longest applicable retention for that file, and legal holds stop destruction.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: A customer may ask for a copy of what they submitted and of the letters Northline sent them. That request is filled within the time in the privacy addendum. Release of the entire claim file, including internal evaluations and attorney communications, is a Legal decision. Intake staff do not email a claim file to a requester because the requester said they were "entitled to it."
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Opening a file, sending the standard acknowledgment, and posting the intake reserve schedule are within every trained First Notice associate's authority. The following require a supervisor before the action is taken:
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss
CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: Quality Review samples at least thirty first notices per week across desks, plus every file in which a department of insurance or a lawsuit alleges that notice was mishandled. A file fails review if the acknowledgment was late without a documented legal reason, if the narrative mixes facts and coverage opinions, if a duplicate was opened, if a representation letter sat unlogged for more than one business day, or if the customer was told the claim would be paid or denied at intake. Failures are coached within ten business days. Three failures of the same type by the same person in a quarter go to the desk manager for a formal plan. Systemic misses, such as an entire storm day of late acknowledgments, are reported to the Chief Claims Officer in the monthly handling report.

text: Agents are audited by Agency Management on a sample of notices they received and the time they forwarded them. An agent who holds notice past the same business day twice in six months is retrained. A third occurrence is referred for appointment review.

text: No employee takes live first notices until they have completed the FNOL module, passed the written scenario exam, and handled five supervised calls or portal filings. Independent adjusters appointed for CAT work complete the short FNOL module before they are given a Northline login. Annual refresher training covers late notice, representation, mortgagee reports, and the current state-addendum changes. Completion is recorded in the learning system. A lapsed refresher suspends authority to open files until it is finished.

The outage log is retained with the claim files.

text: **Example 1. The uncertain leak.** A renter calls and says, "I don't want to file a claim, I just want to know if a dishwasher leak is covered. It happened yesterday and the landlord is angry." The associate opens a claim, explains that opening a file is how Northline looks at coverage, and does not tell the caller that asking the question will raise the premium. The factual narrative records the caller's wish not to pursue payment. If the caller then confirms in writing that they want the file closed and no payment sought, the adjuster confirms there is no third-party injury and no unrepaired damage that creates a later liability, and may close as withdrawn. The notice itself remains in the file.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Example 2. The mortgagee calls first.** A lender reports wind damage at 14 Cedar Street. The named insured has not called. Staff open the property file, capture the loan number, and write to the named insured within two business days. They do not wait for the insured's permission to inspect if the policy gives the mortgagee rights and the property is exposed to further weather. They do not issue the building payment to the lender alone unless CLM-005 says so.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Example 3. The late hail report.** The date of loss is 14 April. The portal filing arrives 2 November, when the insured lists the house. Staff open the file that day, request photos and the inspection from the sale if the insured has it, and assign a property adjuster. They do not send a denial letter from the portal queue that says "reported too late."
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Example 4. The other driver.** A person calls and says a Northline policyholder ran a red light and dented their car. They want the policy limit. Staff open a liability file, collect the other person's damage description, and do not state the limit. If the caller then says "my lawyer will call," staff note it and wait for the letter before any settlement talk. They still send the caller a claim number so the lawyer can find the file.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Example 5. Two policies, one fire.** A fire damages a dwelling insured on a homeowners policy and a jewelry schedule insured on an inland marine policy. Staff open two claim numbers under one event, assign both to the same property adjuster unless workload rules require otherwise, and tell the insured there are two claim numbers and why. Contents under the homeowners policy stay on the homeowners file. The scheduled jewelry does not get paid twice.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

text: **Example 6. The agent who waited.** An agent emails on Thursday that a customer "mentioned a kitchen fire last Friday at the office." Notice reached the Company on the prior Friday. The acknowledgment is already late. The supervisor documents the agent delay, sends the acknowledgment the same day the email is seen, and reports the agent under Section 16. The customer's rights are measured from Friday, not from Thursday.
title: CLM-001 — Claim Submission and First Notice of Loss

topic: Appendix C — Script for the opening of a call
section: Appendix C — Script for the opening of a call
text: The associate says that the call may be recorded, gives their name, and asks how they can help. After the caller describes an event, the associate says: "I am going to open a claim so we have a record and an adjuster can look at your policy. Opening the claim does not mean it has been approved or denied. I will give you a claim number before we hang up." If the caller refuses a claim number and describes only a future, hypothetical event, the associate transfers the call to policy service. If the caller refuses a claim number and describes an event that has already happened, the associate explains that the Company still has to record what it was told, opens the file, and offers the number again. The associate does not argue about premium.

title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: This policy tells adjusters how to decide whether a reported event falls inside a Northline policy. The decision has three parts, and they are answered in order: whether a contract was in force, whether the event meets the insuring agreement, and whether an exclusion, condition, or limit reduces or removes payment. Mixing those parts produces letters that quote an exclusion before anyone has checked that the policy was cancelled, and denials that collapse when the customer points out an endorsement that was never read.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Coverage work is not a hunt for a reason to decline. It is a reading of the contract the customer bought, applied to facts that have been gathered under CLM-003, and written down so a second adjuster can see why the result follows. Where the law of the applicable state limits an exclusion, requires prejudice before a condition can defeat coverage, or imposes a duty to defend broader than the duty to indemnify, that law is part of the analysis. Adjusters do not apply a favorite exclusion from another file, and they do not assume every form in the jacket was issued.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: This document does not authorize the denial letter itself. When the analysis ends in no coverage or in partial coverage, the letter is issued only under CLM-006. When the analysis is uncertain, the file is handled under a reservation of rights or a request for more facts, not under a guessed denial.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Every file with an indemnity reserve, and every report-only liability file that names a potential claimant, receives a written coverage screen. Files opened in error under CLM-001 and closed the same day as non-claims do not. Vendor adjusters may recommend a coverage result. They may not send a denial and they may not tell the customer the loss is covered beyond the authority letter Northline gave them.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Underwriters answer questions about what was sold, what premium was booked, and what form version was issued. They do not direct the claim result on a specific loss. If a coverage dispute reveals that the policy was issued on terms Underwriting did not intend, Claims handles the claim on the policy that was actually issued and refers the form error to Underwriting separately. The customer is not asked to bear a back-office mistake by having the contract rewritten after the loss.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Applicable law.** The state law that governs interpretation of the policy, determined by the policy's choice-of-law clause if it is enforceable, otherwise by the rules Claims Legal publishes in the state addendum. Adjusters do not pick the state with the friendlier exclusion.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Condition.** A policy term that requires the insured to do or not do something, such as give notice, cooperate, or protect the property. A condition is not an exclusion. In many states it defeats coverage only if the Company was prejudiced. The file must say whether prejudice is required and how it is shown.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Endorsement.** A form that changes the jacket. If the endorsement and the jacket conflict, the endorsement controls for the subject it addresses. If two endorsements conflict, the one that more specifically addresses the subject controls. If that test fails, Coverage Counsel decides before any letter goes out.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Exclusion.** A term that takes specified loss, injury, or damage out of an insuring agreement that would otherwise apply. Exclusions are read narrowly when the governing law says so. They are not stretched because the loss is large.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Insuring agreement.** The grant of coverage, including who is an insured, what property or injury is covered, and what perils or legal obligations are covered. If the grant is not met, the analysis stops. Staff do not spend pages excluding a loss that was never covered.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Prejudice.** A concrete harm to Northline's ability to investigate, settle, or defend, caused by the insured's failure. Suspicion is not prejudice. "We would have liked to see the pipe before it was replaced" is prejudice only if the file shows that earlier access would likely have changed the cause or cost, and that the insured's conduct, not Northline's delay, caused the loss of that access.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Reservation of rights.** A written statement that Northline will investigate or defend while telling the insured which terms may later reduce or remove coverage. It is not a denial. The contents and approvals are in CLM-006.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Whole policy.** Declarations, jacket, all endorsements listed on the declarations, and schedules. A form that is not listed and was not delivered is not part of the contract just because it sits in the Company form library.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text:
1. Read the policy that was issued for the date of loss, not the current form and not the renewal that started later.
2. Decide the grant before the exclusion. Decide facts before theory.
3. Ambiguity the Company cannot resolve with the governing-law rules is raised to Coverage Counsel. It is not resolved by choosing the reading that costs less.
4. The customer hears the result in writing, in plain language, with the facts and the policy words that matter. Oral coverage opinions are not the decision.
5. A deductible, a limit, and a coverage denial are different things. Applying a deductible means the loss is covered and the insured shares the first dollars. Calling a deductible a denial misstates the contract.
6. Other insurance, additional insured tenders, and contribution are coverage work. They are not reasons to ignore a Northline insured who has presented a loss.
7. Staff separate "the policy does not cover this" from "we do not have enough facts yet." The second sentence requires a list of what is missing and a date the adjuster will look again.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: The adjuster retrieves the declarations, forms list, and cancellation history for the date of loss from the policy administration system and saves a copy into NCF. A screen print that shows only the policy number and a status of "active" is not the policy. The saved image must show the edition dates of the forms and the limits, deductibles, mortgagees, and listed drivers or locations that apply to this loss.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: If the date of loss falls in a gap between cancellation and reinstatement, the adjuster obtains the notice of cancellation, the proof of mailing, and the reinstatement rules before concluding there is no policy. A reinstatement that the policy or state law makes retroactive puts the policy back in force. A flat cancellation that was processed after the loss because of a billing error does not erase coverage that existed on the date of loss. Those files are referred to a supervisor and to Billing before any no-coverage letter.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: The adjuster lists every person or organization seeking coverage and states why each is or is not an insured. Named insureds, resident relatives, permissive drivers, additional insureds by endorsement, and persons insured by a definition in the jacket are checked against the facts, not against the reporter's assertion. A certificate of insurance that a landlord or general contractor holds is evidence of what the certificate says. It is not, by itself, an endorsement. If the certificate promises additional-insured status and the policy does not contain it, Claims notifies Underwriting the same day. The claim is decided on the policy. Any estoppel or certificate remedy is a Coverage Counsel question, not a front-line assumption either way.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: For personal auto, the adjuster records who was driving, whether that person was listed, excluded by a named-driver exclusion, or using the vehicle with permission, and whether the vehicle is a covered auto. A household member who took the car without permission is not automatically uninsured; the permission facts are written down. A named-driver exclusion is applied only if the signed exclusion is in the policy image and the governing law enforces it.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: For property policies, the adjuster confirms that the damaged building or item is insured property at a described location, or that an off-premises or newly acquired coverage extension applies. A scheduled item stays on its schedule. A business that moved inventory to a new warehouse before the policy was endorsed is examined under the newly acquired or unnamed-location extension, including its day limit and its sublimit. The adjuster does not deny for "unlisted location" without measuring that extension.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: On a named-peril form, the insured must show the loss was caused by a listed peril. On an open-peril or special form, the insured must show accidental direct physical loss to covered property, and Northline must show any exclusion it relies on. The file states which kind of form applies. Adjusters do not call a special-form homeowners policy a named-peril policy because the denial feels easier.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Cause of loss is a fact. "Water damage" is not a cause. The note must say where the water came from: a sudden supply-line break, a repeated leak the insured knew about, surface water, a backed-up drain, wind-driven rain through an opening the wind created, or condensation. Those facts point at different grants and different exclusions. If the cause is not known, the coverage screen says "cause undetermined" and lists the inspection, expert, or test that will determine it. An undetermined cause is not an exclusion.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

topic: 6.2 Liability and the duty to defend
section: 6.2 Liability and the duty to defend
text: On occurrence policies, the adjuster identifies the occurrence, the date, and the claimant's legal theory. On claims-made policies, the adjuster identifies the date the claim was first made, whether it was reported in the policy period or extended reporting period, and whether a prior-knowledge or prior-notice condition applies. Northline's commercial general liability policies in this manual are occurrence forms unless the declarations say otherwise. A claims-made analysis pasted onto an occurrence file is a handling error.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

topic: 6.2 Liability and the duty to defend
section: 6.2 Liability and the duty to defend
text: The duty to defend is broader than the duty to pay a judgment when the governing law uses the complaint-allegation rule or a similar rule. If the complaint alleges a theory that would be covered, and also alleges a theory that would not, the defense is provided for the suit, subject to a reservation that identifies the uncovered theory and any right to recoup defense costs if the governing law allows recoupment and the policy or law supports it. Adjusters do not refuse a defense because they believe the insured will ultimately win, or because they believe the facts are different from the complaint, unless Coverage Counsel has written that the jurisdiction allows a facts-outside-the-complaint decision and the file contains those facts.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

topic: 6.2 Liability and the duty to defend
section: 6.2 Liability and the duty to defend
text: An additional insured's tender is logged the day it arrives. The adjuster compares the endorsement's trigger — for example, liability arising out of the named insured's ongoing operations, or caused in whole or in part by the named insured — to the allegations. A tender that does not meet the endorsement is declined in a letter under CLM-006. Silence for thirty days is not a decision, and it is a service failure.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Physical-damage coverage is analyzed under the collision and comprehensive grants, including the definition of collision and any custom-parts limit. Liability coverage is analyzed under the grant for bodily injury and property damage the insured becomes legally responsible for. Uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage is a first-party contract: the adjuster confirms the tortfeasor's status with the best available evidence, tells the insured what that evidence is, and does not require the insured to sue the tortfeasor before Northline will evaluate the UM claim unless the policy and the state addendum say so. Medical-payments coverage is paid according to its limit and its proof requirements without waiting for a fault decision, unless the form truly conditions it on fault, which the standard Northline personal-auto form does not.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Before an exclusion is cited, the file contains the exact exclusion language, the form number and edition, the fact that meets each element of the exclusion, and a note on any exception to the exclusion that might give coverage back. An exception to an exclusion is a grant. It is analyzed, not skipped. The wear-and-tear exclusion with an ensuing-loss exception is the most common example on property files: the worn pipe itself may be excluded while the sudden water damage that followed may be covered. The adjuster prices those parts separately. Denying the entire kitchen because the pipe was old is a misapplication unless the form and the facts truly put all of the damage inside the exclusion.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Anti-concurrent-causation wording is applied only as written and only as the governing law allows. The adjuster describes each cause and the sequence. A hurricane file that has both wind and flood is not labeled "flood" because flood is excluded. Wind damage to covered property remains covered if the form covers wind, even when flood also occurred, unless the anti-concurrent clause and state law take that wind damage out. Where the causes cannot be separated, the adjuster requests a cause-and-origin opinion before denying the separable portion. CAT files follow CLM-010 for vendor panels and still follow this section for the coverage test.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: The following exclusions are not cited in a denial unless a supervisor, and in the marked cases Coverage Counsel, has agreed in the file:
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text:
| Exclusion or issue | Extra review |
| --- | --- |
| Intentional loss or expected injury, including any inference from a criminal charge | Supervisor. Counsel if a criminal case is open or the insured denies intent. |
| Fraud or concealment after the loss | Supervisor and SIU under CLM-007. A fraud belief alone is not an exclusion analysis. |
| Pollution, bacteria, or fungus, when the loss also involves a sudden break or a fire | Supervisor, because exceptions are common and easy to miss. |
| Business activity inside a homeowners policy | Supervisor. Incidental business and permitted occupancies are checked first. |
| Vacancy | Supervisor. The vacancy definition, the number of days, and any exception for a dwelling under renovation are checked against the facts. |
| Earth movement or flood on a policy that may have a buy-back endorsement | Supervisor confirms the buy-back is absent, not merely forgotten. |
| Assault and battery or liquor liability on a commercial policy | Coverage Counsel if the complaint pleads negligence in addition to the excluded act. |
| Punitive damages | Coverage Counsel. Insurability follows the state addendum. |
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Building-code or ordinance-or-law coverage is paid only when the endorsement is on the policy and the damaged covered property must be repaired under a code the endorsement reaches. The adjuster obtains the code section from the local official or from the contractor's permit set, not from the contractor's unsupported invoice line. Matching of undamaged property — a full roof slope, a run of siding, a floor that crosses a doorway — is decided under the governing state's matching rule and the policy's pair-and-set or part-of-a-pair language. The file cites the state addendum position. Adjusters do not invent a company-wide "we never match" rule.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Tear-out of a building part to reach a broken pipe is covered or not according to the form. Many Northline homeowners forms cover tear-out and replacement of the part that must be removed to access the break, and exclude the pipe itself if the pipe failed from wear. The estimate is split that way. Collapse coverage, if present, is read on its own definition. Not every ceiling stain is a collapse.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Late notice is measured under CLM-001 for the dates and under this section for the effect. The adjuster writes a prejudice analysis: what evidence was lost, why it cannot be reconstructed, and what decision it would have affected. If the property is still available, the witnesses are still available, and the only complaint is that the report came late, prejudice is not established on those facts alone. The condition is then not used as the basis for denial.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Cooperation failures — a refused inspection, a missed examination under oath, a refusal to produce the lease or the maintenance log — are documented with the requests, the dates, and the customer's stated reason. One missed call is not a failure to cooperate. A denial for noncooperation requires the prejudice showing the state requires, supervisor approval, and a letter that tells the insured what remains possible if they cure, if cure is still meaningful.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

topic: 8.2 Protect the property and no voluntary payments
section: 8.2 Protect the property and no voluntary payments
text: The insured must take reasonable steps to protect covered property. Northline pays reasonable make-safe costs when the loss is otherwise covered, and it considers those costs even while coverage is open if CLM-001 authorized them to prevent worsening. An insured who completes permanent repairs before inspection has not automatically forfeited the claim. The adjuster uses photos, invoices, remaining debris, and contractor interviews. If those materials are enough to measure the loss, the early repair is not a defense. If they are not, the file describes what cannot be verified. That gap is a proof problem under CLM-004, and it becomes a condition defense only when the policy and the law support it.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

topic: 8.2 Protect the property and no voluntary payments
section: 8.2 Protect the property and no voluntary payments
text: An insured who pays a third party or makes a repair contract has not, by that act alone, violated a voluntary-payments condition on a liability policy. The condition is aimed at payments and assumptions of obligation that prejudice the defense. Emergency medical transport and minor property mitigation are not treated as a forfeiture. Any denial that cites voluntary payments goes through Coverage Counsel.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

topic: 8.3 Examination under oath and proof of loss
section: 8.3 Examination under oath and proof of loss
text: These tools are requested under CLM-003 and CLM-001, not as a substitute for reading the grant. A late or missing proof of loss is analyzed for prejudice and for waiver. If Northline investigated for months without requesting the proof, a later denial that relies only on the missing form is raised to Coverage Counsel before it is sent, because the Company's own conduct may have waived the condition or estopped the defense.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: The adjuster applies the deductible that matches the coverage part. A wind or hail deductible expressed as a percentage is calculated on the stated insurance amount in the declarations, not on the size of the estimate, unless the form says otherwise. The arithmetic is shown in the file: limit or amount of insurance, percentage, dollar deductible, covered damage, amount payable. Two deductibles are applied to one occurrence only if the policy says two coverage parts each carry their own. Earthquake, hurricane, and named-storm deductibles are not stacked on top of the all-peril deductible unless the form says to stack them. When the wording is unclear, the adjuster applies one deductible, the one the form most clearly triggers, and refers the stacking question to Coverage Counsel if the dollar difference exceeds $10,000.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Payment cannot exceed the limit, but the limit is not a target. Sublimits for jewelry, business property, debris removal, ordinance or law, fungi, and trees are identified before the estimate is agreed. A sublimit is explained in the settlement letter so the customer can see why a $40,000 jewelry schedule did not pay a $40,000 contents list. Additional living expense and loss of rents are limited by the policy's time and dollar terms. The adjuster tracks incurred months against that limit in the file, and warns the insured in writing at the halfway point of a time limit so the end of benefits is not a surprise.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: If another policy may cover the same loss, the adjuster identifies it, tenders or requests the other carrier's position in writing, and continues to handle Northline's own duty. Northline does not tell its insured to "go to the other company first" when the Northline policy is primary. Priority is read from both policies' other-insurance clauses. If both claim to be excess, the adjuster refers the file to Coverage Counsel and, while that question is open, protects the insured's defense and the property. Contribution after Northline pays is Recovery's work under CLM-008. It is not a reason to delay a first-party property payment that Northline owes its own insured.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: A preliminary screen is entered within five business days of assignment for standard files, and within two business days for any file with a defense tender, a fatality, an uninhabitable dwelling, or a reserve at or above $75,000. The screen is updated when new facts arrive. The final screen is completed before the first indemnity payment, before any denial, and before any reservation of rights. A payment issued with no screen is a defect even if the payment was correct.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: The screen uses the NCF coverage template:
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation
CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Template fields left blank are returned by quality review. A screen that says "covered, water" is not a screen.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

topic: 10.3 Talking to the customer while the screen is open
section: 10.3 Talking to the customer while the screen is open
text: The adjuster may explain which coverages are being reviewed and what documents are still needed. The adjuster does not say "we will pay" until the screen supports payment and authority under CLM-005 exists. The adjuster does not say "this is excluded" until the denial is approved. The sentence to use is: "I am comparing the inspection to the water-damage and wear provisions, and I will write you with the result by [date]." A date that the adjuster cannot meet is not offered. If the date moves, the customer is told before it passes, with the reason.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: If the assigned adjuster and the supervisor disagree on the result, the supervisor's view is not silently substituted. Both views are noted, and the claim manager decides. If the amount in dispute exceeds $100,000, or the issue is one of the counsel-review rows in Section 7.2, Coverage Counsel's written advice is obtained first. Counsel's advice is privileged. The factual basis that can be shared with the customer still appears in the letter. Adjusters do not write "our lawyer said no" as the reason given to the insured.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: A good-faith reading later reversed by a court or by an appeal under CLM-009 is corrected prospectively on that file, including payment of amounts due with any interest the law requires. It is not treated as a disciplinary event by itself. A reading that ignored an endorsement that was in the file, or that used the wrong form year, is a handling error and is coached.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Adjusters may complete a coverage screen that results in payment within their payment authority. Any screen that results in a full or partial denial, a reservation of rights, a punitive-damages position, or a refusal to defend is approved under CLM-006 before it is communicated as the Company's position. Independent adjusters submit a recommended screen. The Northline examiner adopts it, changes it, or sends it back. The examiner's name is the name on the decision.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: Quality Review scores coverage screens monthly. A screen fails if it cites an exclusion that is not in the issued form, omits an endorsement that is on the declarations, uses a denial where facts are only incomplete, or shows no prejudice analysis on a condition defense. The target is a fail rate under five percent of sampled screens. Themes from failures are fed back into the quarterly coverage clinic.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: New examiners do not issue denial recommendations until they have completed the coverage module and have had ten screens reviewed without a material miss. Annual training uses real, redacted files, including at least one ensuing-loss file, one additional-insured tender, and one late-notice file in which prejudice was not found. Passing the clinic is a condition of keeping denial-recommendation authority.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: There is no exception to saving the issued policy image in the file. There is no exception to writing the screen before a denial. A catastrophe volume exception may extend the five-day preliminary screen to the time stated in the CAT bulletin, and it may not extend the screen past the point of payment or denial. If NCF is down, the screen is written on the outage template and pasted into NCF the day the system returns.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: CLM-001 opens the file and records the dates this policy uses for notice. CLM-003 supplies the facts the screen is allowed to rely on. CLM-004 prices a covered loss and keeps uncovered items out of the indemnity reserve. CLM-005 pays only what the screen has allowed. CLM-006 sends the denial or reservation. CLM-007 owns fraud and concealment positions. CLM-008 owns contribution and subrogation after payment. CLM-009 owns disagreements the customer raises after the letter. CLM-010 owns catastrophe operations and does not rewrite this coverage test.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Sudden pipe break.** A homeowners special form. The supply line under the kitchen sink splits overnight. The insured shut the water off in the morning and reported the same day. The pipe is twelve years old. The form excludes wear and tear and the pipe itself, and it covers ensuing sudden water damage and tear-out to reach the break. Screen result: partially covered. The estimate removes the pipe cost, pays tear-out and resulting water damage, and applies one all-peril deductible. The letter itemizes the split. It does not call the tear-out a goodwill payment.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Long-term leak.** Same form. The insured noticed staining six months ago, placed a bucket under the sink, and called after the cabinet floor failed. Photos show rot and repeated staining. Result: the sudden-discharge grant is not met for the long-term rot. Any sudden final break is separated if the expert can separate it. The screen does not use the word "neglect" unless the neglect exclusion is in the form and its elements are met. Supervisor review is required because the fungi and wear exclusions both appear in the estimate.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Late hail, no prejudice.** The insured reports hail eight months after the storm, when selling the house. Invoices and photos still show bruising consistent with the storm date, and the roof is available to inspect. Notice was late. Prejudice is not shown. The screen proceeds to cause and to the hail deductible. The late-notice condition is considered and rejected in the screen so the next reader does not reopen it casually.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Additional insured tender.** A general contractor tenders a suit by a subcontractor's employee. The additional-insured endorsement covers injury caused in whole or in part by the named insured's acts in the performance of ongoing operations. The complaint alleges only that the general contractor failed to control its own site, and the facts available show the named insured was not on site that week. The examiner refers the defense question to Coverage Counsel because the jurisdiction's complaint-allegation rule may still require a defense. No denial is sent by the examiner alone.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Certificate with no endorsement.** A landlord produces a certificate stating it is an additional insured. The policy image has no such endorsement and the application did not request one. The screen says the landlord is not an additional insured on the contract. Underwriting is notified. Coverage Counsel is asked whether the certificate plus the agent's email creates an estoppel issue before a denial is sent to the landlord. The named insured's own coverage is analyzed separately and is not held up by the landlord's tender.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text: **Two deductibles.** Wind damages the dwelling and hail dents the detached garage on a policy with a two-percent wind-hail deductible on the dwelling and a flat deductible on other structures. The adjuster computes each deductible as the form states, shows the math, and does not also take the all-peril deductible. If the form is ambiguous about whether the percentage applies to the garage, one deductible — the reading more consistent with the state addendum — is applied and the dollar difference is noted for counsel if it exceeds $10,000.
title: CLM-002 — Coverage Verification and Policy Interpretation

text:
- [ ] Policy image for the date of loss is saved in NCF, including endorsements and cancellation history.
- [ ] The form year in the screen matches the image, not the current jacket.
- [ ] Every person seeking coverage is accepted or rejected with a reason.
- [ ] Cause of loss is specific, sourced, and dated.
- [ ] The insuring agreement is answered before any exclusion.
- [ ] Each exclusion relied on is quoted, and any exception is answered.
- [ ] Exclusions that were considered and rejected are listed.
- [ ] Conditions include a prejudice paragraph where the law requires one.
- [ ] Deductible math is shown.
- [ ] Sublimits are identified before settlement.
- [ ] Other insurance is either ruled out or tendered.
- [ ] The result matches what the customer will be told.
- [ ] Denial or reservation, if any, is routed to CLM-006 and is not already promised on the phone.
- [ ] Counsel-review items are actually with counsel.
- [ ] A diary exists if the result is "facts insufficient," with the missing items named.

title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Coverage and payment depend on facts the Company can explain. This policy states how those facts are gathered: site inspections, photographs, recorded statements, documents, experts, medical examinations, and examinations under oath. It also states what staff may not do in the name of investigation. An investigation is finished when the remaining unknown facts are unlikely to change the coverage result or the dollar amount, not when every imaginable record has been collected.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Northline investigates claims it has opened under CLM-001. It does not investigate people for reasons unrelated to the claim. It does not use the claim file as a reason to enter a home beyond the loss, to record a person secretly, or to contact a represented person directly. Fraud indicators are referred under CLM-007. Ordinary investigation stays with the adjuster.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: The assigned adjuster owns the investigation plan. Independent adjusters and experts work inside that plan and inside their assignment letters. Defense counsel owns investigation of litigated liability once counsel is assigned, and coordinates with the adjuster so the claim file and the litigation file do not diverge. A fact counsel learns that affects coverage, reserves, or injury value is sent to the adjuster the week it is learned, subject to any privilege note counsel places on the message.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: This policy covers first-party property, first-party auto, and third-party liability. Workers' compensation, if ever written by a Northline affiliate, is outside this manual. Health records are requested only when the claim puts the person's medical condition in issue, and only with the authorization or legal process Section 8 requires.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Examination under oath (EUO).** A formal statement taken under the policy's oath condition, with a transcript, after notice of the topics and after the person has had a fair chance to attend with a representative. It is not a recorded telephone interview.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Expert.** A person retained for a technical opinion the adjuster is not qualified to give: cause and origin, engineering, building code, accident reconstruction, medical specialty review, or a forensic accountant on a business-interruption loss. A contractor who writes an estimate is a vendor under the repair program, not an expert, unless retained for a cause opinion.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Independent medical examination (IME).** An examination by a physician Northline retains, used on a bodily-injury claim when the treating records are not enough to evaluate the injury the claimant has put in issue. It is not a treatment relationship.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Inspection.** A first-hand look at the damaged property, vehicle, or scene, done by an adjuster or by a person the assignment letter authorizes, with photos and measurements stored in NCF.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Recorded statement.** An audio statement taken with notice to the speaker that it is being recorded, where the law allows recording with that notice. A surprise recording is not a recorded statement under this policy. It is a violation of it.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Spoliation.** The loss or destruction of evidence that a person had a duty to keep. The Company can commit it by failing to preserve a vehicle, a part, or a file, and an insured or claimant can commit it by discarding property after being told to keep it. The response is a documented prejudice analysis, not an automatic denial.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text:
1. Ask for the evidence that can change the result. A long list sent to look thorough is a delay.
2. See the property when sight would change cause or cost, unless a documented exception in Section 6 applies.
3. The file distinguishes observation from conclusion. "The shingles are creased across the south slope" is an observation. "This is hail from the April storm" is a conclusion and needs the reasons.
4. People are told why a statement, document, or examination is being requested and what policy term, if any, requires it.
5. One missed appointment is rescheduled. Noncooperation is a pattern plus prejudice, analyzed under CLM-002, not a label applied after a single no-show.
6. Evidence is stored in NCF. Photos on a phone that never upload are treated as if they do not exist, and the adjuster who lost them owns the recovery effort.
7. Investigation respects the home. Adjusters do not open drawers unrelated to the loss, comment on housekeeping except as it bears on cause, or bring an unexpected second person into a home without telling the occupant who that person is and why they are there.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Within two business days of assignment on a standard file, and the same day on a fatality, an uninhabitable dwelling, a large-loss file, or a defense tender, the adjuster writes a short plan in NCF:

text: The plan is updated when a new theory appears. It is not a script the adjuster must exhaust if an earlier step already answered the question. A kitchen-supply-line break with clear photos, a plumber's invoice, and an agreement on price does not need an engineer. A collapsed roof does.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Preservation comes first when the evidence can disappear. Examples: a vehicle about to be repaired, a pipe fitting the plumber intends to discard, security video that a store overwrites in seven days, and a commercial machine that will be put back into service. The adjuster sends a written hold the day the risk is known, identifying the item and asking that it be kept until inspection or until the adjuster releases it in writing. The hold is specific. "Keep everything related to the claim" is not a useful hold and is not used on consumer files. It may be used, more specifically detailed, on a commercial loss with counsel's help.
