text: Liability scenes are inspected when a view would affect fault or notice of a hazard: a fall on a step, a lighting claim, a commercial parking lot, a vehicle with disputed damage. A minor parking-lot door ding with consistent photos does not need a site visit if the drivers agree on the event.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: The adjuster offers two appointment windows within five business days of assignment for local files, or within the CAT bulletin's time for catastrophe files. The occupant is told who will attend. Inspections are done during reasonable hours unless the loss is an emergency make-safe. The adjuster arrives with identification. They do not enter if the only person present is a minor. They do not comment to neighbors about the insured's claim. Measurements, roof access, and moisture readings follow the safety rules in the field manual. No adjuster walks a roof they are not equipped and authorized to walk. Drone or ladder-assist vendors are used instead, and the limitation is noted so a later reviewer knows the roof was seen, and how.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: The note is written the day of the inspection or the next business day. It includes arrival time, who was present, weather if it matters, a room-by-room or elevation-by-elevation description, measurements, materials, cause observations, temporary repairs already done, habitability, and a list of photos with what each photo shows. "See photos" is not a note. The note also records what the occupant said on site, labeled as their statement, and any disagreement about scope. If the adjuster cannot determine cause, the note says so and recommends the expert. It does not fill the gap with a guess.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Photos must show the overall scene, the specific damage, a reference for scale, and any pre-existing condition the estimate will exclude. Metadata is preserved. Photos are not edited except for a brightness correction that is disclosed. A photo with a circle or arrow may be added as a second copy; the original stays.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Auto physical-damage inspections use the approved appraisal network unless the vehicle is not drivable, in which case a field appraiser or tow-yard inspection is assigned. The appraisal records point of impact, prior damage, odometer, options, and whether the vehicle appears a total loss under the total-loss rule in CLM-004. Tear-down is authorized only when a hidden-damage question cannot be answered otherwise, and the authorization is in the file before the shop opens the vehicle. Parts removed in a tear-down are held until the adjuster releases them.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: A recorded statement is taken when fault, permission, occupancy, the timeline, or the cause would otherwise rest on a single unrecorded conversation. It is not taken as a ritual on every file. Before the recording starts, the adjuster identifies everyone on the line, states that the call is being recorded, states the claim number, and asks the speaker to confirm they are willing to give the statement. If the speaker declines, the adjuster continues the investigation with other evidence and notes the refusal. A single refusal is not, by itself, noncooperation.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: The statement covers the facts of the event, the property or injury, other insurance, and prior similar losses only as those points relate to this claim. It does not cover unrelated medical history, immigration status, or the person's finances except where the policy condition makes finances relevant, such as a business-interruption claim or a scheduled-property ownership question. Minors are not asked to give recorded statements. A parent may describe what a young child said, and that description is labeled as secondhand.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: If a lawyer or public adjuster represents the speaker, the statement is scheduled through the representative. The representative may attend and may object to questions. They may not coach on the recording. If coaching makes the statement useless, the adjuster stops, notes what happened, and raises the next step — usually an EUO or a written question list — with a supervisor.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: An EUO is requested only when the policy provides for it and one of the following is true: the loss facts are materially inconsistent and ordinary statements have not resolved them; documents that the policy requires have been withheld after a specific request; SIU has concurred that an EUO is the right tool under CLM-007; or Coverage Counsel recommends it on a coverage question that turns on the insured's knowledge. An EUO is not used to wear a claimant down, and it is not requested on a third-party claimant who has no EUO condition in any contract with Northline.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: The request is in writing, gives at least ten business days' notice unless the person agrees to an earlier date, states the place or the video method, and describes the documents to bring. The insured may have a lawyer present. Northline does not object to that. The examiner is a person trained to take EUOs or is Coverage Counsel. The assigned adjuster may attend. A transcript is ordered and placed in the file. The insured may obtain a copy under the policy term or the state addendum. After the EUO, the adjuster writes what was learned that the investigation did not already know. An EUO that changes nothing is not repeated.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Witnesses are contacted once, politely, and told they are not required to speak unless a legal process requires it. Their statement is recorded only with permission. Neighbors are not told the insured's limits, reserve, or medical details. If a witness is hostile or is a minor, the adjuster stops and asks a supervisor before a second attempt. Surveillance of a claimant is not ordered by an adjuster. It is an SIU or defense-counsel tool, approved under CLM-007 or by the litigation supervisor, and it is used only when the injury claim and the observed activity cannot be reconciled any other way. Adjusters do not follow claimants in their own cars.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Requests are specific: "the plumber's invoice for the 12 March visit and any photos the plumber took," not "all documents related to your home." The requester gives a reasonable date and a way to send the file electronically. Personal phones of employees are not the destination for medical records or tax returns.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Medical records and bills are requested with an authorization that names Northline, the claim, and the providers, or by a legal process in litigation. The authorization is not bundled into a general release. Records are used to evaluate the injury claimed. They are not used to look for unrelated conditions to embarrass a claimant. Staff who need to discuss records use the minimum necessary. Mental-health, substance-use, and sexual-health records are requested only when the claimant has put that condition in issue, and the request is approved by a bodily-injury supervisor.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: A claimant may use their own treating physician. Northline does not require an IME before it will review those records. An IME is appropriate when the diagnosis, the cause, or the duration conflicts with the mechanism of injury or with the bills in a way the records do not explain, and the conflict is material to the value. The examiner is board-certified in the relevant specialty, has no treating relationship on this claim, and is told to give an opinion, not to advocate. The claimant receives the appointment details, travel reimbursement under the state addendum, and a copy of the report if the law or the negotiation requires it. One IME is the norm. A second requires the bodily-injury manager's approval and a reason the first was insufficient.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: An expert is hired when a technical question is material and beyond the adjuster's training. Cause of a large fire, structural movement, the source of water in a wall, accident reconstruction with serious injury, and the measurement of business interruption beyond a simple payroll ledger are typical. An expert is not hired to bless a decision the adjuster has already announced to the customer. The question is written before the expert is retained: "Did wind create an opening that allowed rain in, or did rain enter through a pre-existing gap at the flashing?" A question that says "confirm the exclusion" is sent back.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Experts come from the approved panel unless a manager approves an off-panel expert because of geography or specialty. The assignment letter states the question, the facts provided, the documents provided, the deadline, and the fee cap. Staff do not withhold a document that cuts against the Company's preferred result. The expert's report must separate facts, methods, and opinions. Draft reports that the adjuster rewrites are not the expert's work and are not allowed. Clarifying questions may be sent in writing and saved to the file.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: If the expert's opinion supports coverage, the file follows the opinion unless a second expert is retained for a stated methodological reason, approved by a manager. Shopping for a contrary opinion without that reason is a handling defect. If two experts disagree, the adjuster describes both methods and a manager decides which method is more reliable, or the file is compromised with that disagreement disclosed in the reasoning. The customer is not told "our expert disagrees with yours" without the substance.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Expert fees are an expense reserve under CLM-004. They are proportionate to the amount and the question. A $6,000 engineering review on a $2,500 disputed item requires supervisor approval before it is ordered. The approval note explains the coverage consequence, not the desire to win.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: On third-party claims the adjuster gathers the facts needed to evaluate legal responsibility under the law of the place of the accident. Police reports are requested. They are not treated as conclusive. The insured driver and the claimant are both asked for their account. Physical evidence — point of impact, skid marks, vehicle locations, weather, signals — is recorded. Comparative fault is analyzed in percentages the jurisdiction uses, and the percentage is explained. A demand package is compared to that evaluation. It is not answered with a token offer that ignores the documents.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Northline does not admit liability to a third party until the coverage screen supports indemnity and the liability evaluation supports responsibility. "We are sorry this happened" is acceptable. "Our insured was at fault and we will pay whatever you want" is not. Any partial admission is consistent with the later negotiation under CLM-005.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: For premises claims, the adjuster obtains the incident report, maintenance records for the relevant period, photos of the condition, and the names of employees who were present. Those records are preserved the day the claim is known. A later "the video already overwritten itself" note is a failure if no hold was sent when the claim arrived.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: A file is not left in "investigation" with no outstanding request and no scheduled activity. Supervisors run a report of files with no activity for fifteen days and clear the report weekly. If the only delay is a third party who will not respond, the file shows the attempts and the decision that was made with the evidence on hand, or a supervisor-approved decision to wait longer because the missing item is essential and still likely to arrive.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Staff do not alter photos, backdate notes, or delete a note that later looks inconvenient. Corrections are a new note that identifies the error. System timestamps stay as they are. A customer who points out a factual mistake receives a correction if they are right, and an explanation if they are not. Estimates of value and reserve comments are internal. They are still written as if they could be read by a regulator or a court, because sometimes they are. Sarcasm, comments about a person's appearance, nationality, or character, and medical guesses by non-medical staff are prohibited. "Claimant was limping and then walked normally to a car" may be a fair observation if it was actually seen and is relevant. "Claimant is faking" is a conclusion the adjuster may not write. The referral path for that concern is CLM-007.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Any employee may collect documents and schedule an inspection. Retaining an off-panel expert, ordering an IME, noticing an EUO, and ordering surveillance require the approvals named in this policy. Adjusters leave a property if they feel unsafe, report the situation to their supervisor, and reschedule with appropriate arrangements. They do not attempt to prove cooperation by staying in an unsafe place. Law enforcement is called for an active threat. The claim is not discussed with the officer beyond what is needed for safety, unless the policy or a legal duty requires a report of a specific crime, in which case the adjuster calls SIU and a supervisor first unless waiting would create immediate danger.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Quality Review samples inspection notes and investigation plans every month. A file fails if the plan is missing on a severe file, if photos claimed in the note are not in NCF, if a document request is a blanket demand, if an EUO was noticed without the predicate in Section 7.2, or if a represented person was contacted directly. Field ride-alongs occur at least twice a year for staff adjusters in their first two years. Independent adjusters are scored on note quality and photo standards. Repeated failure removes the adjuster from the Northline assignment list until retraining is complete.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: Training for new adjusters includes a supervised inspection, a recorded-statement workshop, and a module on medical-authorization limits. No adjuster notices an EUO until they have observed one and completed the EUO workshop. Annual refreshers use examples of spoliation and of expert questions written the wrong way.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: A CAT bulletin may change inspection timing and may allow desk adjustment. It may not waive photo standards, preservation holds, or the ban on secret recording. A life-safety emergency may postpone a full inspection note by one business day while make-safe work is arranged. The note then explains the postponement. There is no exception that allows a denied-access assumption after only one unanswered call.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: CLM-001 sets first notice and proof-of-loss timing. CLM-002 uses the facts gathered here and decides prejudice. CLM-004 turns measurements into dollar amounts. CLM-005 does not pay a disputed scope that this policy says was never investigated. CLM-006 is the path for a noncooperation denial. CLM-007 receives fraud referrals and owns surveillance approvals with the litigation supervisor. CLM-009 covers a customer's challenge to an expert or an IME. CLM-010 may change field deployment and does not change evidence integrity.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

topic: The pipe that was thrown away
text: **The pipe that was thrown away.** The plumber replaced a failed angle stop and discarded the part before the adjuster called. The adjuster does not deny the claim for spoliation on that fact alone. The plumber's description, the invoice, the new part, and the water pattern may be enough. The note records what was lost and why the remaining evidence is or is not sufficient. A preservation hold is sent the same day for any remaining wet materials if cause is still open.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **One missed inspection.** The insured misses Tuesday's appointment and calls Wednesday to apologize. The adjuster offers two new times. The file does not say "failure to cooperate." If the insured then refuses three written offers over three weeks without a reason, the supervisor reviews a cooperation analysis under CLM-002.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Represented insured.** A public adjuster writes that all contact must go through the office. The adjuster schedules the inspection through that office and still expects the insured, or a person with keys and authority, to allow access. The public adjuster may attend. The adjuster does not refuse to inspect because a public adjuster is involved, and does not agree to the public adjuster's scope on site without measuring.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Expert question done poorly.** An adjuster emails an engineer: "Need you to confirm wear and tear so we can deny." The supervisor cancels that instruction. The replacement question is: "Identify the source of water that stained the ceiling. State whether the discharge was sudden or long-term, and the observations that support that timing." Both emails stay in the file so the correction is visible.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Medical scope.** A claimant treats for a wrist fracture after a rear-end collision and also mentions a ten-year-old back surgery in passing. The adjuster requests the wrist records and the emergency-room record. The old back-surgery chart is not requested unless the claimant is now claiming a back injury from this accident. The bodily-injury supervisor approves any broader request.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text: **Video hold.** A grocery store reports a fall the day it happens. The adjuster sends a hold that afternoon identifying the date, the approximate time, and the camera covering the aisle, and asks that the recording be kept for thirty days or until copied. A hold sent three weeks later, after the store's loop has overwritten the footage, does not cure the gap. The file then uses the incident report and witness accounts, and the delay is a handling miss.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

text:
- [ ] Date, arrival time, and people present are recorded.
- [ ] The note was uploaded within one business day.
- [ ] Observations are separated from conclusions.
- [ ] Measurements and materials needed for the estimate are included.
- [ ] Photos match the note and show overall and close views.
- [ ] Originals are unedited; marked-up copies are labeled.
- [ ] Habitability and any make-safe need are stated.
- [ ] The occupant's on-site account is attributed to them.
- [ ] Unresolved cause questions name the next step, not a guess.
- [ ] A preservation hold went out the same day if evidence was at risk.
- [ ] No comment in the note mocks the customer or states a medical or fraud conclusion.
- [ ] The investigation plan is updated to show what this visit closed and what remains.
title: CLM-003 — Investigation, Inspection, and Evidence

section: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement
text:
| Field | Value |

| Title | Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement |
| Owner | Chief Claims Officer, jointly with the Chief Financial Officer |
| Approved by | Claims Governance Committee and the Reserve Committee |
| Effective date | 15 November 2026 |
| Next review | 15 November 2027 |
| Version | 4.0 |

| Applies to | All lines listed in CLM-001 |

title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: A reserve is the Company's best current estimate of what it will ultimately pay on a file, plus the expenses it will incur to handle the file. An estimate is the measurement of a property or vehicle repair. They are related and they are not the same. This policy tells adjusters how to set both, how to change them, and how to keep uncovered damage out of an indemnity number. Finance uses the aggregate of case reserves, with its own bulk and incurred-but-not-reported provisions, to state the Company's liabilities. A reserve that is posted high "so nobody asks" and a reserve that is posted low "until we are sure" both distort that statement. Neither is allowed.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Customers are not told the reserve. The reserve is not a settlement offer and it is not an admission. Settlement authority lives in CLM-005 and is set from the evaluation, which should sit inside the reserve, not above it.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: This policy applies to every open indemnity claim and to expense reserves on files that will incur outside cost. Bulk reserves, catastrophe loads, and actuarial IBNR are Finance's responsibility. Adjusters do not post IBNR on a file and do not reduce a case reserve because they heard the accident year is redundant. Reinsurance reporting thresholds are in Section 11. Meeting a reinsurance trigger is not a reason to understate a reserve, and avoiding a trigger is not a reason to overstate one.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Independent adjusters recommend reserves and write estimates. Northline examiners post the reserve. An estimate prepared by a contractor or a public adjuster is evidence of cost. It becomes Northline's measurement only when an adjuster adopts it or reconciles it line by line.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Case reserve.** The file-level estimate of future indemnity payments and, separately, future loss-adjustment expense, as of today. It includes amounts already recommended but not yet paid. It is reduced when payments are made only in the sense that the remaining reserve equals the new ultimate estimate minus what has been paid. Staff do not "use up" a reserve by paying and forgetting to reset the ultimate.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Expense reserve (ALAE).** Allocated loss-adjustment expense the file will incur: independent adjusters, engineers, defense counsel, court reporters, IMEs. Unallocated company overhead is not reserved on the file.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Incurred.** Paid plus remaining case reserve. A reserve change that does not change the ultimate estimate of the loss is a reallocation between paid and outstanding, not a new view of the claim. The note should say which one it is.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Estimate.** A line-item measurement of the cost to repair or replace damaged covered property, using the approved estimating platform, current local price lists, and the scope the inspection supports.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Betterment.** A deduction for the difference in value between a new item and the item that was damaged, taken only when the policy or state law allows depreciation or betterment and only on items that are actually improved. It is documented item by item.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Total loss.** A vehicle or other property whose repair cost plus projected supplements meets or exceeds the total-loss threshold in the state addendum, or whose structural damage makes a safe repair unreasonable even below that threshold.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Stair-stepping.** A pattern of small reserve increases that track payments already decided, instead of an honest ultimate posted when the facts were known. Stair-stepping is a defect even if the final paid amount is correct.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text:
1. The reserve matches the current evaluation. If the evaluation moves, the reserve moves in the same work session.
2. Post the ultimate, not the next payment. A roof that will cost $18,000 is reserved at the expected payout, not at the $2,500 emergency advance.
3. Indemnity and expense are reserved separately and coded to the right coverage part.
4. Uncovered damage is not reserved as indemnity. If coverage is in doubt, the reserve reflects the probability-weighted outcome or the conservative probable outcome the Reserve Committee specifies for that line in the current reserve bulletin. The bulletin is followed. Personal caution is not a second method.
5. Depreciation, deductibles, and salvage are applied in the evaluation the way the payment will apply them, so the reserve is a forecast of the check, not of the contractor's gross estimate.
6. Nobody lowers a reserve to hit a financial target. Nobody raises a reserve to justify a settlement they are not otherwise prepared to explain.
7. Reserve notes state facts and numbers. They do not advocate.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: At first notice, before the investigation has produced an estimate, the opener posts the intake reserve from the current schedule published by the Reserve Committee. The schedule sets amounts by line, peril, and a small set of severity flags: injury reported, airbag deployment, dwelling uninhabitable, commercial operations interrupted, attorney representation already in hand, and fatality. The schedule is a starting point, not a cap. If the caller describes a loss that is obviously larger — a total commercial building fire, a tractor-trailer fatality — the opener posts the schedule amount and immediately refers the file to a supervisor to set a realistic initial reserve the same day. Leaving a total-loss house fire at the $5,000 intake default overnight is a reserve failure.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: The assigned adjuster replaces the intake reserve with an evaluated reserve within ten business days of assignment, or within three business days after the inspection, whichever is earlier. Liability files with no medical information use the injury-pending reserve in the schedule and a diary to obtain bills. A liability file is not left at the intake number for sixty days because "we have no records yet" if a demand, a hospital admission, or a lawyer's description of surgery is already in the file. Those facts support a higher placeholder and a plan to refine it.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: A zero indemnity reserve is allowed only when the coverage screen concludes there will be no payment, or when the file is truly report-only and the note explains why no claimant and no injury exist. A zero reserve is not used to park a file the adjuster has not read.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: The estimate includes only damaged property related to the covered cause, plus operations the policy covers, such as reasonable tear-out, debris removal, and code items the coverage screen has allowed under CLM-002. Pre-existing damage is listed and excluded, with photos. Undamaged property is included only when the matching rule or the policy requires it, and the line cites that rule. The adjuster does not add items to avoid an argument, and does not omit items the photos show because the customer was difficult.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Measurements follow the inspection note. If the estimate and the note disagree, the estimate is wrong until the note is corrected or the estimate is brought back into line. Unit costs come from the approved price list for the ZIP code and the month. Manual overrides are allowed for a documented local condition — a material shortage, a historic material, a necessary specialty trade — and the override reason is on the line. A global increase of every line by a percentage, to "be fair," is not an override. It is an unpriced negotiation and it belongs in settlement authority, not inside the estimating platform.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Overhead and profit are included when the repairs require coordination of three or more trades, or when the state addendum requires them more broadly. They are not included on a single-trade repair that a homeowner or one contractor can do without a general contractor, unless the insured reasonably incurs general-contractor cost and the addendum treats that cost as part of the loss. Sales tax is applied where the work is taxable. Labor minimums and trip charges are used as the platform intends, once per trade per visit, not once per room as a way to increase the total.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Where the policy pays actual cash value until repair is complete, the adjuster calculates depreciation by item, using age, condition, and useful life. A flat percentage applied to the whole estimate is allowed only for a contents list of many small items of similar age, and the percentage is explained. Recoverable depreciation is released under CLM-005 when the insured documents that the repair or replacement was done. The first payment letter states the actual-cash-value amount, the recoverable amount, and what proof will release it. Nonrecoverable depreciation is identified as such so the customer is not told to send receipts for money the policy will not return.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Contents estimates use the insured's inventory, photos, and, when needed, a sampling method a supervisor approves. The adjuster does not demand receipts for every ordinary household item on a total-contents fire. Proof is proportionate. High-value items, scheduled property, and items the insured did not own are documented more strictly. The adjuster asks where an item was kept and who owns it when the occupancy is shared. Commercial business-personal-property estimates use the insured's records. A forensic accountant is considered under CLM-003 when the records and the claim diverge by more than the examiner's authority or when the interruption claim is based on projected sales rather than history.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Code items are estimated only after CLM-002 allows them, and only to the code section in the file. Matching lines cite the state rule. If the adjuster believes matching is owed and the supervisor disagrees, Section 11 of CLM-002 on internal disagreement applies. The reserve follows the view that is currently the Company's evaluation, and it is changed the day that view changes. The difference is not left off the reserve because an appeal might fail.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Repair estimates use the approved network's labor rates and procedures unless a documented deviation is approved. Betterment on tires, batteries, and wear items is taken only under the state addendum. The adjuster audits for unrelated prior damage and for operations that the photos do not support. Supplements are reviewed within three business days. A supplement that changes the repair method — weld versus replace, structural versus cosmetic — is inspected or photo-documented before approval.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Total-loss values use the approved valuation guide for the local market, adjusted for documented condition, mileage, and options. A comparable-vehicle list is saved in the file. Tax, title, and transfer fees are included or excluded exactly as the state addendum requires. The insured is shown the valuation before the total-loss payment is issued, and is given a fair chance to submit comparables the guide missed. Salvage handling follows CLM-008. The reserve on a likely total loss is the expected settlement plus fees, minus expected salvage only if the reserve method in the bulletin says to net salvage. The current bulletin nets expected salvage on auto physical damage and does not net it on property until salvage is certain.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Bodily-injury reserves are built from liability, damages, and coverage, in that order. The note states the fault percentage, the medical specials to date, a reasonable projection of future care if the records support one, wage loss supported by employer confirmation or a reasonable documented estimate, and general damages consistent with the jurisdiction and the injury. The evaluation is a range, and the reserve is the expected outcome inside that range, not the top of the range and not the plaintiff's demand. Demands are recorded. They are not copied into the reserve field.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: A surgery recommendation that no surgeon has made is not reserved. A surgery that has been recommended in writing by the treating physician is reserved at a reasonable cost unless a contrary IME, approved under CLM-003, supports a different figure. Future care that is possible but unlikely is described and is not reserved at one hundred percent. The reserve bulletin tells the examiner whether to use expected value or a stated percentile for that uncertainty. Examiners follow the bulletin.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Property-damage liability is reserved at the supported repair or total-loss figure, plus documented rental or loss of use for a reasonable period. Loss of use is not reserved at the claimant's asking rate if that rate exceeds the local market and the addendum allows a market measure. Comparative fault reduces the indemnity reserve on the liability file. It does not reduce a first-party collision payment unless the policy is one of the uncommon forms that makes collision fault-based. The standard Northline collision form is not fault-based.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Defense counsel's liability view is considered and is not a substitute for the examiner's reserve. If counsel values the case differently, both numbers are in the file and the claim manager reconciles them within five business days. Until then the higher number is carried if the difference is an indemnity exposure the Company may have to pay, so the reserve is not light while the debate continues. The reconciliation note explains the final choice.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: A reserve is revised the day the evaluation changes: a new medical bill of consequence, a supplement, a coverage decision, a liability percentage change, a demand that reveals previously unknown injury, a denial, or a settlement recommendation. The note states the old ultimate, the new ultimate, and the fact that moved it. Changes of more than $25,000, or more than twenty-five percent of the prior indemnity reserve when the prior reserve exceeds $10,000, require supervisor approval before or the same day they are posted. Changes that cross a reinsurance threshold require the notice in Section 11 and supervisor approval regardless of size.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Closing a file without payment requires the reserve to be taken to zero with a reason that matches the closure code: denial issued, withdrawn, no contact after the attempts CLM-001 requires, or paid in full. Closing a file at a residual reserve to "keep it warm" is not permitted. If more payments are likely, the file stays open.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Reopening follows CLM-001. The reserve is posted again on the day of reopen at the new expected cost, not left at zero until someone remembers.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Reducing a reserve because a payment was made, without reconsidering the ultimate, is the ordinary paid-to-outstanding movement and needs only a one-line note. Reducing a reserve because a manager asked the team to "watch severity" is prohibited. Any such request is reported to the Chief Claims Officer and the Chief Financial Officer. Good-faith revisions after new facts are not that request, and staff are not punished for raising a reserve when the facts require it.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Payment authority in CLM-005 and reserve authority are aligned but not identical. An adjuster may post a reserve up to the reserve limit for their role even when the payment will later need a higher approver, so the balance sheet is not waiting on the approver's calendar. The current limits are:
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text:
| Role | Reserve limit (indemnity ultimate) | Estimate approval |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claim associate | $5,000 | Desk estimates within the bulletin |
| Adjuster | $25,000 | Standard property and auto estimates |
| Senior adjuster | $75,000 | Includes supplements within the limit |
| Claim supervisor | $150,000 | Overrides and matching disputes |
| Claim manager | $500,000 | Large-loss estimates with the large-loss unit |
| Vice President, Claims | Above $500,000 | Any file referred by the large-loss unit |
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: A person may not split a loss into pieces to stay inside a limit. One occurrence is one authority test, even if it is paid in several checks. Expense reserves have a separate limit at one half of the indemnity limit for the role, and defense-counsel budgets above $25,000 go to the litigation supervisor regardless of that fraction.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Any file whose indemnity reserve reaches $250,000, any fatality, any suit seeking class treatment or extra-contractual damages, and any loss that meets a treaty reporting trigger is reported to the large-loss unit and to Reinsurance the day the threshold is crossed. The large-loss unit reviews the evaluation within five business days. Reinsurance notices are factual. They are not an invitation for the reinsurer to direct the claim. Settlement strategy stays with Northline, subject to any treaty right the Reinsurance department actually confirms in writing. Adjusters do not call reinsurers directly.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: A clash notice is made when several files from one event may aggregate. The event number from CLM-001 is the key. CAT aggregations follow CLM-010 as well as this section.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: The Reserve Committee reviews development quarterly: initial reserve versus reserve at ninety days versus ultimate paid, by line and by office. Persistent under-reserving at first evaluation, defined as a median upward development above the Committee's threshold, results in a revised intake schedule or in coaching, not in a quiet instruction to pad. Persistent over-reserving is treated the same way. Individual files are referred to quality review when a reserve moves more than three times in thirty days without a change in facts, when a payment exceeds the reserve that was on the file the day before with no same-day increase, or when depreciation is a flat rate the note cannot explain.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Estimates are audited against photos on a sample each month. Unsupported line items are removed and the estimator is coached. A pattern of unsupported lines removes estimating authority until retraining. Public-adjuster and contractor estimates that were accepted without a reconciliation are an automatic fail if the difference from Northline's figure exceeded $5,000.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: Customers are told the measurement of their covered repair: the scope, the price, the deductible, the depreciation, and the net payment. They are not told "your reserve is $18,000." If a customer asks what the Company "has set aside," the adjuster explains that internal accounting figures are not the settlement and then returns to the estimate. The estimate is shared. Hiding the scope while asking the customer to accept a check is not permitted. Disputes about price are handled by comparing line items, by a second inspection when the dollar gap justifies it, and by the appraisal condition when the policy provides appraisal and CLM-009 says it is time to offer it. They are not handled by silently moving the reserve to the customer's number.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: No employee posts a reserve above the intake schedule until they have completed the reserve module and have had five evaluated reserves reviewed. Estimators complete the platform certification for their line. Annual training covers stair-stepping, depreciation, and the difference between a demand and an evaluation, using redacted files from the prior year.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: There is no financial-close exception that allows a reserve change to be held until the next month. If the system is unavailable on the last day of a month, the outage log records the evaluations that must be posted first when the system returns, and Finance is told the same day which large files are affected. A CAT bulletin may authorize a simplified intake reserve for the first seventy-two hours. It may not authorize leaving that simplified number in place after the inspection.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: CLM-001 requires an intake reserve the day the file opens. CLM-002 decides which dollars are covered before they enter the indemnity estimate. CLM-003 supplies the measurements and the expert opinions the estimate relies on. CLM-005 pays inside the evaluation this policy produced and releases recoverable depreciation. CLM-006 removes indemnity reserves when a denial is issued, leaving expense if work remains. CLM-007 may change an evaluation when SIU finds material misrepresentation. CLM-008 handles salvage credits. CLM-009 handles appraisal and other disputes about the number. CLM-010 sets CAT estimating rules and price-list deviations during a declared event.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text:
| Version | Date | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.0 | 1 June 2022 | Separated reserve policy from payment policy. |
| 3.3 | 15 January 2025 | Added reinsurance notice at $250,000 after a late clash report. |
| 4.0 | 15 November 2026 | Defined stair-stepping as a defect; required same-session reserve changes; prohibited target-based reserve moves; clarified net-salvage practice; required line-item depreciation. |
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Intake then evaluation.** A homeowner reports a kitchen water loss. Intake posts the schedule amount of $7,500. Three days later the inspection supports $11,200 of covered tear-out and repair, a $4,800 pipe item that is not covered, and a $1,000 deductible. Depreciation is $900, of which $700 is recoverable. The indemnity reserve becomes $11,200 minus $1,000 minus $900, or $9,300, plus a note that $700 may return if repairs are completed. The uncovered pipe is not reserved. Posting $16,000 "for the whole estimate" is wrong. Posting $7,500 still, because the check has not been requested, is also wrong.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Stair-step.** An auto injury file is reserved at $5,000. The adjuster then receives records of a fracture and physical therapy and pays $5,000, raises the reserve to $8,000, pays $3,000 more, and raises it again when a lawyer sends a demand. The facts for a $25,000 evaluation were in the first set of records. The pattern is stair-stepping. The supervisor resets the method and coaches the adjuster. The cure is not to jump the reserve to an unsupported $100,000.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Do not follow the demand.** Counsel for a claimant demands $450,000. Specials are $22,000, the fracture has healed, and fault is agreed. The examiner's range is $60,000 to $85,000. The reserve is set at $75,000 with the range explained. It is not set at $450,000 to match the letter, and it is not set at $22,000 to match the bills and ignore general damages.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Total loss arithmetic.** The valuation is $14,200. The state addendum requires sales tax and title fees of $980. Expected salvage is $2,100 and the bulletin says to net salvage on auto. The reserve is $14,200 plus $980 minus $2,100, or $13,080, until salvage is actually received. If salvage later brings $1,600, the ultimate is revised. The customer sees the valuation and the fees. The customer is not shown an internal salvage credit as if it were a charge against them beyond the contract.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Manager pressure.** A supervisor tells a team to cut open property reserves by ten percent before quarter-end because results look heavy. The team does not comply. The supervisor's instruction is reported. Files are reviewed for genuine over-reserves based on facts, which may be reduced, and the reductions are documented one file at a time.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text: **Code item not yet allowed.** A contractor includes $6,400 to bring an undamaged electrical panel to current code. The coverage screen has not allowed ordinance coverage. The $6,400 stays off the indemnity reserve and off the payable estimate. It may be listed in the customer explanation as not covered, with the reason. If the screen later allows it, the reserve moves the same day.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

text:
- [ ] Indemnity and expense are separate.
- [ ] The ultimate, not the next check, is what the number represents.
- [ ] Deductible, depreciation, and excluded scope are visible in the math.
- [ ] The fact that changed the number is named when the reserve moves.
- [ ] The figure is inside the poster's reserve authority, or the approver is identified.
- [ ] Reinsurance and large-loss notices were sent if a threshold was crossed.
- [ ] The customer-facing estimate matches the covered scope inside the reserve.
- [ ] The note contains no joke, no comment on the person's character, and no reference to a financial target.
- [ ] A zero reserve has a closure or coverage reason.
- [ ] Liability reserves state fault, specials, and general damages, and do not copy the demand.
title: CLM-004 — Reserves, Estimating, and Loss Measurement

title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: This policy governs how Northline pays a claim once coverage and measurement support a payment. It covers who may approve a check, who must be named on it, what a release may and may not say, when depreciation is returned, and how liability claims are settled without selling the insured short or paying a demand the evaluation does not support. Payment is the part of the claim the customer can spend. A correct coverage decision that is paid to the wrong person, or held for weeks after the amount is agreed, is still a bad claim.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Speed does not outrank accuracy. A payment that has to be stopped, reversed, or reissued because the payee was wrong costs the customer time and costs the Company a handling defect. The rules below are the ordinary path. They are not a reason to withhold an undisputed amount while a disputed amount is still open.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: This policy applies to indemnity payments and to claim-specific expenses paid through the claim system. Premium refunds, agent commission, and vendor invoices for non-claim work are outside it. Structured settlements and Medicare reporting are in Sections 10 and 11. Catastrophe advance payments follow this policy plus the CAT bulletin under CLM-010. Nothing here authorizes payment of an item the coverage screen has rejected. If the screen and the requested check conflict, the check waits and the screen is corrected or the request is withdrawn.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Undisputed amount.** The portion of a covered loss that Northline has already measured and does not contest, even if other portions remain open. On a property file it is often the agreed repair items. On a bodily-injury file it may be a documented medical bill the evaluation already accepts.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Dual payee.** A check payable to more than one person because each has a legal interest, such as the insured and a mortgagee, or the insured and a contractor the insured has asked to be named.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Release.** A written surrender of claims, used on third-party settlements and on certain first-party disputes. A standard first-party property payment is not conditioned on a general release of all policy rights.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Holdback.** Recoverable depreciation or a retained amount the policy allows Northline to pay after repairs are complete. It is not a bargaining chip.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Authority.** The largest indemnity payment, or series of payments on one occurrence, that a role may approve. Authority is personal. It is not borrowed by asking a colleague who is out of the office to "just sign."
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text:
1. Pay the undisputed amount. Do not hold it hostage to the open dispute.
2. Name every person the policy or the law makes a necessary payee. Do not name people for convenience.
3. The check amount matches the settlement letter. Verbal deals are written down the same day and sent to the customer before or with the payment.
4. A release is no broader than the dispute being settled. First-party customers are not asked to release extra-contractual rights or future claims as the price of a sum the policy already owes.
5. Authority is checked against the whole occurrence. Splitting checks to stay under a limit is a violation, even if each check would have been proper at a higher authority.
6. Payment dates are kept. If a promised date will be missed, the customer is told before the date, not after the complaint arrives.
7. Staff do not ask a customer to return a payment that was correctly issued because a later reinspection changed someone's mind, except where the payment was a documented overpayment caused by a factual error or fraud. Ordinary estimate changes on unrepaired items are handled in the next payment, not by clawing back funds the customer received in good faith for items Northline agreed.

text: An advance for make-safe work authorized under CLM-001 may be issued before the final screen when delay would increase the damage. The payment note states that the advance is subject to the coverage decision and will be credited to any later settlement. If coverage is later denied, recovery of the advance is pursued only when the customer was told, before the work, that repayment might be requested and the governing law allows recovery. It is not pursued against a customer who was told the Company would protect the property and who spent the money on that protection in good faith, unless fraud is established under CLM-007.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Payment is made to the named insured unless this section requires someone else to be added. If there are two named insureds, both are named unless one has given a written direction that the other may receive payment alone, and the payment does not affect a mortgagee. A direction signed under pressure, or signed by a person the adjuster has reason to believe does not understand it, is not accepted. The adjuster may require both payees on the check and let them endorse it together.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: If the policy's mortgage clause applies and the payment is for real property, the mortgagee is named on any payment at or above the threshold in the current payment bulletin. The current threshold is $10,000 for dwelling or building payments, and any payment of any size if the mortgagee has notified Northline of a default or has requested to be named. Payments only for contents, additional living expense, or a scheduled item that is not part of the building are not made payable to the mortgagee. The adjuster confirms the mortgagee's name and address with the policy image or with a written payoff statement. A check to a misspelled lender is a defect.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: When a dual-payee check will be difficult for the insured to negotiate, the adjuster may, with the mortgagee's written consent, pay the contractor directly for completed work, or pay into an escrow the mortgagee accepts. Consent is saved in the file. Verbal consent from a local branch employee who cannot bind the lender is not enough. Until consent arrives, the dual-payee check is the default, and the adjuster explains to the insured why the lender is on the check.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

topic: 6.3 Lienholders on vehicles and other property
section: 6.3 Lienholders on vehicles and other property
text: A perfected lien on a vehicle is protected according to the state addendum. Total-loss payments name the lienholder and the insured in the manner the addendum requires. The adjuster obtains a payoff figure good through a stated date and does not rely on a figure the customer remembers. Repair payments on a financed vehicle are made to the insured and the shop, or to the insured alone, as the addendum and the repair agreement provide. They are not made to the auto lender unless the lender has a right to the repair check under the contract and the addendum.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: If a lawyer or public adjuster has a valid written authorization to receive proceeds, the check may name the representative and the client as the law and the agreement require. Northline does not pay a representative alone unless the authorization expressly allows it and no mortgagee or lienholder is omitted by doing so. Northline does not calculate a public adjuster's fee and does not increase the loss to cover that fee. The fee, if owed, is a matter between the customer and the representative. Staff do not advise the customer whether the fee is fair. They do not refuse to issue the customer's payment because they disapprove of the hiring.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Payments to a minor that exceed the small-sum threshold in the state addendum are not made payable to a parent personally. They are paid under the method the addendum allows: a restricted account, a guardianship, or a court order. Below the threshold, payment to the parent as natural guardian is allowed only if the addendum says so, and the file contains the parent's identification and a statement of the relationship. Estate payments require letters of appointment that are still in effect. A surviving spouse is not assumed to be the personal representative.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Make-safe vendors and repair shops are paid when the insured has assigned the proceeds in writing or has signed a direction to pay, and the work billed matches the approved estimate. Northline does not pay a vendor for work the inspection does not support because the vendor threatens a lien. The insured is told about the dispute and the approved amount is paid according to the payee rules. Any lien process is referred to Legal when papers are served.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: When scope is agreed on part of a loss and genuinely disputed on the rest, the agreed part is paid within the timeline in Section 9. The letter identifies what is paid, what is still open, and what will resolve the open part. The customer is not required to sign a full release to receive the agreed part.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: The actual-cash-value payment is issued without waiting for repairs, once the measurement is done. Recoverable depreciation is paid after the insured submits proof that the covered repair or replacement was completed. Proof is invoices, photos of completed work, or a contractor's completion certificate. The adjuster reviews that proof within ten business days and either pays the holdback or writes what is missing. The holdback is not denied because the customer used a different contractor, chose a reasonably equivalent material, or spent less than the estimate. If the customer spent less, the holdback is limited to the amount actually and reasonably incurred above the actual-cash-value payment, unless the policy and the state addendum require payment of the full replacement cost regardless. The Northline homeowners form pays replacement cost incurred. It does not pay a windfall above the cost incurred. The letter says this in plain language when the holdback is requested.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: A time limit in the policy for completing repairs is enforced only after the adjuster has confirmed the limit applies, has warned the insured before it expires, and has considered a reasonable extension for permit delays, contractor shortages, or a catastrophe. Extensions are given in writing. A denial of holdback solely for lateness requires supervisor approval under CLM-006.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Every offer is inside an evaluation written under CLM-004. The first offer on a bodily-injury claim is a good-faith offer based on that evaluation, not a token. The Company does not open at a fraction of a known value to "leave room." Negotiation may move within the range. Movement above the range requires a revised evaluation and the authority that matches the new number. A demand above the policy limit is handled with the excess-exposure rules in Section 8.3.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: A third-party release identifies the parties, the event, the claim number, and the amount. It releases bodily-injury claims or property-damage claims or both, as the payment intends. It does not release claims the payment does not cover. A property-damage settlement does not include a hidden bodily-injury release when the person has treated and those bills are unpaid, unless the person is represented and the release is explicit. Minors' releases follow Section 6.5. A release of a lienholder's interest is obtained when the settlement is meant to clear that lien.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: First-party disputed amounts — a fight about price, not about whether any coverage exists — may be resolved with a dispute-specific release that states the items closed and the items left open. A first-party release that waives the appraisal right, the right to recoverable depreciation, or the right to complain to a regulator is not used. Regulatory complaint rights cannot be waived by a release in any event, and staff do not imply that they can.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: When a liability evaluation, a demand, or a suit approaches the policy limit, the examiner notifies the insured in writing of the limit, the demand, and the insured's right to retain personal counsel at the insured's own expense to advise on excess exposure. If a limits demand is made with a reasonable time to respond, and the liability and damages evaluation support paying the limit, the file is referred the day the demand arrives to a claim manager for a limits decision. Letting a limits demand expire without a documented decision is a serious handling failure. Contribution from other policies is pursued under CLM-002 and CLM-008 and does not excuse a missed demand deadline on Northline's own limit.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Defense is not withdrawn because the limit has been tendered unless the policy and the governing law allow withdrawal and Coverage Counsel agrees. Any such step is communicated to the insured before it happens.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

topic: 8.4 No admission as a bargaining tool
section: 8.4 No admission as a bargaining tool
text: Releases may say the payment is not an admission of liability where that is accurate. They are not conditioned on the claimant agreeing to a fact the claimant disputes. Confidentiality clauses are not requested on ordinary claims. They require Legal's approval and a real reason, such as a settlement with a minor celebrity exposure or a commercial dispute the parties have both asked to keep quiet. A confidentiality clause is never used to stop a customer from talking to a regulator.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: A structured settlement is considered when the claimant is a minor, has a permanent injury, or asks for periodic payments, and the amount is large enough that the structure market can serve it. The claimant is encouraged to consult their own adviser. Northline uses approved annuity issuers. The present value of the structure plus any cash portion equals the agreed settlement. Structures are not used to obscure the amount, and they are not forced on a claimant who wants a lump sum the evaluation supports. Documents are reviewed by Legal before funding.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

topic: 11. Medicare, Medicaid, and other benefit rights
section: 11. Medicare, Medicaid, and other benefit rights
text: When a bodily-injury settlement involves a person who is or may be a Medicare beneficiary, the examiner follows the Company's Section 111 reporting procedure and resolves known Medicare conditional payments before or at settlement, as that procedure and federal law require. Staff do not promise a claimant that Medicare "does not need to know." Medicaid and ERISA plan liens that have been asserted in writing are addressed in the settlement. A lien that has not been asserted is not invented, and a lien that has been asserted is not ignored. Questions about the validity of a lien go to Legal. The injured person is not pressured to sign a release that leaves them alone with a lien the settlement was supposed to resolve, unless they are represented and the release makes that allocation explicit.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: The default is electronic payment to a verified account or a check mailed to the address on the policy or to an address the payee has confirmed in writing. A change of address requested only by telephone is confirmed by a callback to the prior number of record or by a written request. Staff do not reroute a payment to a new account because of a single email, and they do not accept wiring instructions that conflict with the payee rules in Section 6. Suspected diversion is reported as a security incident the same day and the payment is held until the payee is re-verified. That hold is explained to the insured if they are reachable by a known number.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Cash is not paid. Gift cards are not paid. A payment is not handed to an agent to "pass along" unless the payee has authorized that delivery in writing and the agent signs a receipt the same day. The receipt is imaged into NCF.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: When Northline pays more than the policy owes because of its own arithmetic error, Claim Accounting is told and the customer is given a clear letter. Repayment is requested. It is not demanded in a tone that suggests fraud. If the customer disputes the overpayment, the file goes to a supervisor. Recovery from a customer who spent an erroneous payment in good faith on the repairs Northline approved is waived unless the amount exceeds $2,500 and a manager approves the recovery attempt. Overpayments caused by misrepresentation are handled under CLM-007 and may be recovered in full.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: A stop-payment is requested the day a check is lost, stolen, or issued to the wrong payee. The replacement waits until the stop is confirmed. Two live checks for the same item are a serious defect. The person who issues the second check without a stop confirmation is responsible for the recovery effort together with their supervisor.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Approvals are recorded in NCF under the approver's own credentials. Sharing a password so a payment can "go out tonight" is a conduct violation. Out-of-office authority is delegated in the system, not by text message. The delegate uses their own limit or the specific temporary limit that was granted, whichever is lower. A temporary limit is logged and expires on a stated date.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: Quality Review samples payments each month for payee errors, releases that were too broad, undisputed amounts that were held, authority splits, and missing settlement letters. Any payment to a wrong mortgagee is a priority fail and is corrected within two business days after discovery. Trends are reported to Claim Accounting and to the Chief Claims Officer.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: New adjusters issue no payments above the associate limit until they have completed the payee module, including mortgagee and minor exercises. Annual training includes a wire-diversion scenario and a limits-demand scenario. Failing the limits-demand scenario suspends authority to handle demands above $50,000 until the person retakes it successfully.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: A CAT bulletin may allow a flat advance of a stated amount before inspection. The advance still requires a payee check and a claim number. It is credited to the final payment. There is no exception that allows a release of future claims in exchange for an undisputed payment. There is no exception that allows cash. A same-day emergency housing advance for an uninhabitable dwelling may be approved by a supervisor outside ordinary hours, documented the next business day, and paid to the insured or directly to a lodging provider with the insured's consent.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: CLM-001 identifies mortgagees and representatives at intake. CLM-002 and CLM-004 decide what is owed. CLM-006 governs any decision to pay nothing. CLM-007 governs holds and recoveries based on fraud. CLM-008 governs salvage and subrogation credits that are not deductions from a customer's first-party payment unless the policy says so. CLM-009 governs disputes after a payment or an offer. CLM-010 governs catastrophe advances.

text: **Undisputed roof, disputed interior.** Wind damage to a roof is agreed at $16,400 after the deductible. Interior staining is still under investigation because cause is not settled. The roof payment is issued within five business days. The letter says the interior is open. No release is requested. Holding the roof check until the interior engineer reports is a violation unless the engineer question could show the roof itself is not covered, and that possibility is documented.

text: **Mortgagee spelling.** The declarations say "First Harbor Bank, ISAOA." The adjuster adds the bank on a $22,000 dwelling check using that name and the mailing address from the policy image, confirmed by the bank's payoff letter. A check made only to the insured because the insured said the loan was "almost paid off" is a defect. The payoff letter settles the question.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Depreciation release.** The insured replaces a roof for $1,100 less than the replacement-cost estimate and sends the invoice and photos. Northline pays recoverable depreciation up to the amount incurred, not the full holdback above the actual cost. The letter shows the math. The adjuster does not refuse the holdback because the shingle brand differed from the estimate when the replacement is of like kind and quality.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Limits demand.** A claimant's lawyer demands the $100,000 bodily-injury limit within fourteen days and encloses medical records of a surgery. The evaluation supports the limit. The examiner notifies the insured the day the demand arrives and refers the file to a manager that day. The manager's decision is recorded before the fourteenth day. A diary set for the thirteenth day with no evaluation in the file is a handling failure even if someone pays on the last afternoon.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Release too broad.** An adjuster agrees to pay a disputed fence invoice and sends a release of "all claims, known or unknown, arising out of the policy." The supervisor withdraws that release. The replacement text closes only the fence item for the stated date of loss and states that additional living expense, if any remains, is unaffected.
title: CLM-005 — Claim Payments, Settlements, and Releases

text: **Wrong account.** An email from a public adjuster gives new wiring instructions that do not match the direction to pay on file. The adjuster does not wire the funds. The adjuster calls the insured at the number already in the file, confirms the payee, and reports the email as a possible diversion. The payment goes out only after that confirmation, by the method Section 12 allows.

title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: A denial tells a customer that Northline will not pay a claim or a part of a claim, and it tells them why in language they can answer. A reservation of rights tells an insured that Northline will investigate or defend while specific policy terms remain in question. These are different letters. They protect different interests. Using a denial when the facts are incomplete, or using a reservation as a soft denial that freezes the claim, violates this policy.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: This document sets the content, the approvals, and the timing of both letters. The coverage reasoning itself is done under CLM-002. The investigation that supports the facts is done under CLM-003. This policy does not create a new reason to decline. It controls how a reason already found is communicated and who must agree before it is communicated.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Every full denial, partial denial, refusal to defend, and reservation of rights on a Northline claim is issued under this policy. A courtesy explanation that a particular item is outside an estimate — for example, an unrelated rot item the adjuster removed from a water-loss scope — is a partial denial if Northline is refusing to pay an item the customer claimed. It is written as one, even if the rest of the claim is being paid. A note in the estimate with no letter is not enough when the customer asked for the item.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Closing a file as withdrawn, because the insured stated in writing that they do not want to pursue payment and no third party is affected, is not a denial. Closing a file as "no contact" is not a denial either. It is a closure under CLM-001 and it may be reopened. Staff do not use a no-contact closure to avoid sending a denial they have already decided.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Third-party claimants are told when Northline will not pay them, for example because the insured is not legally responsible or because no coverage applies to the insured. The letter to a third party does not dump the insured's private coverage analysis. It states the result that affects the third party and the factual basis at a level the third party is entitled to hear. Coverage Counsel reviews the form of that letter when the reason is a coverage defense rather than a liability evaluation.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Denial.** A written decision that no payment will be made for the claim, or that no defense will be provided.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Partial denial.** A written decision that pays some of what was claimed and refuses the rest, including a refusal based on a sublimit, an exclusion of part of the damage, or a finding that part of the damage was not caused by the covered event. A deductible is not a partial denial. It is an application of a limit on payment and is explained in the payment letter under CLM-005.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Reservation of rights.** A written notice that Northline will continue to handle the claim or the defense, and that specified terms may later defeat or limit coverage. It preserves a defense only to the extent the governing law allows. It is not a finding that the insured breached the policy.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Prejudice finding.** The factual conclusion, required in many states before a condition can support a denial, that the Company was harmed in its investigation or defense. The finding is written under CLM-002 before this policy's letter is approved.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Reconsideration.** A second look at a denial because the customer supplied new facts, a new legal point, or a complaint. Reconsideration is handled under Section 10 and, if the customer frames it as an appeal, under CLM-009.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text:
1. The letter is specific enough that the customer can gather the facts or the policy language that would change the result.
2. Every reason the Company is actually relying on is in the letter. Reasons held back for later are treated as waived if the jurisdiction would treat them as waived. Adjusters do not keep a private second theory "in case we need it."
3. Reasons the Company is not relying on are omitted. A letter that quotes five exclusions in the hope that one will stick is a defective letter.
4. The tone is direct and respectful. The customer is not told they were foolish to report the claim, and they are not praised while being denied in a way that obscures the decision.
5. No denial is issued orally. If a customer asks on the phone, the adjuster says the decision will be in writing and when it will be sent.
6. A reservation is sent as soon as the Company has a good-faith question, not after months of unconditional handling that may waive the question.
7. Undisputed covered amounts are paid under CLM-005 even when a partial denial or a reservation addresses other amounts.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: A denial may be approved only when all of the following are in the file:

CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: A denial is not permitted because the customer was rude, because the loss is frequent, because the premium is small relative to the claim, or because the producer asked Claims to "protect the book." Those facts may be referred to Underwriting for a separate renewal decision after the claim is decided on its merits. They are not coverage facts.

text: The letter does not say "based on the information you provided" without saying what that information was. It does not accuse the customer of fraud unless SIU has approved that allegation and Legal has approved the wording. It does not predict litigation. It does not say the customer "failed to read their policy."

text: Partial-denial letters itemize. An itemized table — claimed item, decision, reason — is required whenever more than one item is refused or whenever the refused amount exceeds $2,500. The table uses the customer's descriptions where possible so they can find the line.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: A reservation is issued when Northline will take an action that could be treated as an admission of coverage if done in silence, and a specific coverage question remains open. Typical triggers:
