text: A reservation is not issued on every file. A routine water loss that is clearly covered does not need one. Sending a reservation "to be safe" on every claim trains no one and frightens customers. If there is no specific term to cite, there is no reservation.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: The reservation identifies each policy term that may apply, the fact that raises the question, and what Northline will do next. It states that the insured may hire their own lawyer at their own expense to advise on coverage, and that Northline's defense counsel, if one is appointed, defends the lawsuit and does not give the insured coverage advice. It asks for information the Company still needs. It is sent within ten business days after the trigger appears, and in all events before or with the first defense action. A reservation sent after the Company has defended for months without one is referred to Coverage Counsel to assess waiver before anyone relies on it.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: The insured is not asked to sign the reservation and return it. Acknowledgment is not a condition of handling the claim. If the insured disagrees with the reservation, the disagreement is noted and the claim continues. The disagreement is not treated as a failure to cooperate.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: When the question is resolved in favor of coverage, the adjuster sends a short letter that withdraws the reservation and states the result. Leaving a reservation in place after the question has been answered is a defect. When the question is resolved against coverage, the reservation is followed by a denial that meets Section 6, or by a partial denial, and defense is ended only if the law and Coverage Counsel allow it. The insured receives the denial before defense counsel withdraws, with enough time for the insured to arrange their own defense as the addendum or the court requires.

text: The approver reads the screen and the letter. Approval is not "see above" forwarded from a queue. If the approver changes the reasoning, the screen is updated so the file and the letter match. A letter that is stricter than the screen, or a screen that is stricter than the letter, is returned.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Independent adjusters may recommend. They do not sign Northline denial letters and they do not tell the customer "this will be denied" while the recommendation is pending.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: A denial or reservation is sent as soon as the file is ready under Section 5, and no later than the state-addendum deadline. Where the addendum is silent, the Company standard is fifteen business days after the Company has the information it reasonably needs, and in no event more than forty calendar days from notice without a written explanation to the customer of what is missing and why it matters. That explanation resets the conversation. It does not reset the deadline forever. If the missing item is not essential, the decision is made on the evidence in hand.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Sending a denial early to "stop the clock" before the inspection is complete is prohibited unless the missing inspection cannot change the result — for example, the policy was cancelled months before the loss and the cancellation notice is already proved. The file must say why further facts would not matter.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: A customer may ask Northline to reconsider by writing to the address in the denial letter or by filing an appeal under CLM-009. New facts are investigated promptly. The original approver does not decide the reconsideration alone if the customer has submitted new documents or has alleged that a fact in the letter is wrong. A second reviewer at equal or higher authority reads the file. The result is a new letter: the denial stands, the denial is modified, or the denial is withdrawn and payment is made. The new letter is sent within fifteen business days after the new information is complete, or the customer is told what is still needed.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Reconsideration is not an argument. The second reviewer may agree with the first decision. The customer is still entitled to see that the new material was addressed. A one-line "we stand by our denial" that ignores a new expert report is a failed reconsideration.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Payment after a reversed denial includes the amounts owed and any interest the state addendum requires, calculated from the date the amount should originally have been paid. The interest calculation is shown. Staff do not describe interest as a goodwill gesture when it is required.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: A denial that is late, that omits the real reason, that cites the wrong form, or that ignores documents in the file creates a risk beyond the policy limit. Adjusters flag that risk to a manager when they see it on a file they inherit. They do not hide an earlier bad letter by writing a worse one. The repair is a corrected letter, a reconsideration, and, if a suit or a department complaint is likely, notice to Coverage Counsel. Bad-faith labels are not applied by adjusters to their own Company in customer correspondence. The facts are stated to counsel plainly, including the mistake.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: Every denial above $100,000 and a monthly sample of all other denials are reread by Quality Review against the screen, the policy image, and the letter. A letter fails if it cites language not in the issued form, if it omits an itemized partial denial, if it denies on a condition without the prejudice finding, if a reservation was required and was not sent, or if the tone accuses the customer without an SIU finding. Failed letters are corrected within five business days if the decision itself was wrong, or coached if only the drafting was wrong. A corrected decision is communicated to the customer. Coaching without a correction, when the decision was wrong, is not the remedy.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: New senior adjusters complete the denial workshop and have five draft letters rewritten with a supervisor before they may approve a partial denial. Annual training uses one overturned denial from the prior year, with names redacted, so the same miss is not repeated. The workshop includes the difference between a deductible explanation and a partial denial, because that confusion is a repeated source of complaints.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: There is no volume exception that allows a denial to go out without the approver reading it. During a catastrophe, CLM-010 may assign additional approvers. It does not lower the content standard. A denial may be sent by email or portal if the customer has agreed to electronic communication or has filed electronically. A paper copy is also mailed when the state addendum requires mail, or when the electronic message bounces. The file records both attempts.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: CLM-001 forbids intake staff from denying claims. CLM-002 is the analysis this letter expresses. CLM-003 is the factual support. CLM-004 requires the indemnity reserve to be removed when a full denial is issued, except for amounts still possible on reconsideration. CLM-005 pays the undisputed portion of a partial denial. CLM-007 supplies the only route to a fraud denial. CLM-009 is the appeal path named in the letter. CLM-010 does not create a summary denial process.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text:
| Version | Date | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.0 | 1 June 2022 | Separated denial procedure from coverage interpretation. |
| 4.0 | 15 November 2026 | Required itemized partial denials; prohibited oral denials and unused alternative theories; set reservation triggers and withdrawal letters; required a second reviewer on reconsideration with new facts; added interest on reversed denials. |
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Not ready.** The adjuster believes a roof leak is long-term wear. The only support is a single photo of staining, and the roof has not been inspected because the insured has been out of town. A denial is not approved. A status letter asks for an inspection date. The sentence "we are unable to cover long-term leaks" is removed from the draft.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Partial denial done correctly.** The screen allows sudden water damage and tear-out, and excludes the failed supply line. The letter pays the tear-out and the resulting damage, denies the pipe, quotes the wear exclusion and the ensuing-loss exception, and attaches a two-line table. The deductible explanation is in the payment paragraph, not in the denial paragraph. The customer can appeal the pipe decision without delaying the check for the tear-out.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Reservation on a mixed lawsuit.** The complaint alleges both negligent maintenance, which the liability form may cover, and a knowing pollution discharge, which the pollution exclusion may remove. Defense is assigned. A reservation goes out within ten business days identifying the pollution exclusion and the allegations that raise it. The letter does not deny the claim. Defense counsel is told not to advise the insured on the exclusion. When the pollution count is dismissed and the remaining count is covered, the reservation is withdrawn in writing.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Late notice with prejudice unproved.** Notice was four months late. The property is still there and witnesses are available. A denial based on notice is not approved. If other terms defeat the claim, they are evaluated on their own. The notice issue is recorded as considered and rejected so it does not reappear in the letter as a makeweight.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Fraud wording.** SIU reports inconsistencies in an inventory. SIU has not concluded that the insured misrepresented a material fact. The denial draft says "you fraudulently inflated your claim." The manager removes that sentence. The letter, if a denial is otherwise proper, is limited to the valuation and coverage points that are proved. A fraud denial waits for CLM-007.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Reconsideration with a new report.** After a wear denial, the insured sends an engineer’s report that the discharge was sudden and that staining the adjuster called long-term was dye from a repair the same week. A second reviewer, not the original approver alone, orders a reread of the photos and the new report. The result letter addresses the engineer’s points one by one. If the new report is more reliable, the denial is withdrawn and interest is calculated. If it is not, the letter says why the method was less reliable, in terms a non-engineer can follow.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text: **Third party.** Northline concludes its insured was not negligent in a parking-lot impact, based on the scene photos and both statements. The letter to the third party says the Company will not pay because the investigation shows the insured did not cause the impact, and it summarizes the facts. It does not attach the insured's recorded statement or discuss the insured's limits. If the third party later sues, the file is handled as a suit under CLM-001, not as a reason to pretend the letter was never sent.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

text:
- [ ] The decision word is accurate: denial, partial denial, or reservation. One letter does not blur them.
- [ ] The policy image matches every quotation, including edition dates.
- [ ] Facts are specific and sourced in the file, even if the letter itself is written in plain sentences.
- [ ] No exclusion is cited that the screen rejected.
- [ ] No extra exclusion is cited "in the alternative."
- [ ] Condition denials include prejudice where the law requires it.
- [ ] Fraud is not alleged unless CLM-007 and Legal approved the words.
- [ ] Partial denials are itemized when more than one item is refused or the amount exceeds $2,500.
- [ ] Undisputed sums are paid, not held.
- [ ] Appeal rights and any required appraisal or department language are included.
- [ ] A direct phone number is on the letter.
- [ ] The approver required by Section 8 has read the screen and the letter.
- [ ] A reservation that is no longer needed has been withdrawn.
- [ ] The indemnity reserve matches the letter the day it is sent.
title: CLM-006 — Denials, Partial Denials, and Reservations of Rights

title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Most claims are honest. Some contain mistakes, some contain exaggeration, and a smaller number contain deliberate misrepresentation. This policy tells claim staff how to recognize a concern, how to refer it, and how to keep handling the honest parts of a file while the Special Investigation Unit does its work. It also tells SIU what it may decide and what must go to Legal or to a claim manager before the customer hears the word "fraud."
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Northline does not use fraud procedures to win ordinary coverage disputes. A weak claim, a confused inventory, or a customer who is angry is not a fraud file. Mislabeling it as one injures the customer and, because regulators read these files, injures the Company. The reverse is also true. A file with a serious, specific inconsistency is not kept on the ordinary desk because the adjuster is uncomfortable making a referral.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: This policy is an internal control. It is not a description of techniques for committing fraud, and it is not a set of scripts for deceiving a claimant. Staff follow it and stop.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Every Northline employee and every vendor adjuster who handles a Northline claim must refer concerns as this policy requires. SIU accepts referrals on first-party and third-party claims. SIU does not investigate employees except through the separate corporate investigations process, and it does not investigate producers except together with Agency Management and Compliance. A claim that also involves a suspected dishonest employee is referred to both places the day the employee issue appears. The claim referral does not wait for the employee investigation to finish.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Law-enforcement reporting is decided by SIU leadership with Legal, under Section 10. Adjusters do not call a police department to report a customer for fraud on their own authority.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Material misrepresentation.** A false statement of fact, made in connection with the claim, that a reasonable insurer would consider important to coverage or to the amount payable. An error the customer corrects when asked, a difference of opinion about value, and a statement that is wrong but unimportant to the result are not material misrepresentation under this policy.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Concealment.** A deliberate withholding of a fact the policy or a specific question required the person to disclose. Failure to volunteer a fact nobody asked about is evaluated under the policy wording and the law. It is not automatically concealment.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **SIU hold.** A system status that stops indemnity payment until a manager releases it. It does not stop make-safe work that prevents further damage, and it does not stop a defense that CLM-002 requires, unless Coverage Counsel approves a different course.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Referral.** A written transfer of a concern to SIU with the facts that prompted it. A referral is not an accusation. The customer is not told "you have been referred for fraud."
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Indicator.** A fact that, alone or with others, justifies a referral. Indicators are not proof. Proof is SIU's conclusion after an investigation that meets Section 7.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text:
1. Refer facts, not hunches about the kind of person the customer is. Nationality, neighborhood, accent, and demeanor are not indicators and are not written in the referral as if they were.
2. The ordinary claim continues. Undisputed amounts that are unrelated to the concern are paid unless a manager documents why payment would compromise the investigation.
3. Staff do not entrap, do not invent a pretext for a call, and do not secretly record a conversation. Recorded statements follow CLM-003.
4. The customer is not accused in a note, a letter, or a conversation unless a fraud denial has been approved under Section 9 and CLM-006.
5. Mistakes are allowed to be mistakes. The first response to an inconsistency is usually a plain question.
6. SIU independence matters. The unit reports to the Head of Special Investigation, not to the desk that wants a denial. Claim management may not order a particular SIU outcome.
7. Confidentiality is tight. Referral contents are not discussed with agents, underwriters, or other claimants beyond what that function must know. Underwriting may be told the claim outcome after it is final, through the ordinary underwriting-referral path, not through informal comment.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

topic: 5.1 Ask before referring, when it is safe to ask
section: 5.1 Ask before referring, when it is safe to ask
text: When a single fact does not match — a date, a mileage, an item on an inventory — the adjuster asks the customer for an explanation in a normal claim question. "The shop report shows 62,000 miles and the application shows 41,000. Can you help me reconcile that?" is the right tone. The customer's explanation is written down. If the explanation resolves the point, there is no referral and the note says the point was resolved. If the explanation creates a larger inconsistency, or if the customer refuses to address a specific material point, the adjuster refers.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

topic: 5.1 Ask before referring, when it is safe to ask
section: 5.1 Ask before referring, when it is safe to ask
text: The adjuster does not ask a series of trick questions designed to produce a contradiction. The adjuster does not confront a customer with an accusation to "see how they react." Reaction is not evidence.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: The adjuster refers the file the same business day any of the following is present. The referral does not wait for the adjuster to build a case.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text:
- A document appears altered, or two official documents state inconsistent material facts and the customer, after one plain question, cannot account for the difference.
- The customer asks Northline to pay for property that a prior inspection, a photo, or an independent record shows was not damaged in this event, and the dollar amount is material.
- A bodily-injury claim describes a mechanism that the medical records contradict in a way that is not a matter of medical opinion — for example, treatment records dated before the alleged accident — after the dates have been checked for a clerical error.
- The same property or the same injury is claimed with another insurer for the same event and the customer denied the other claim when asked.
- A fire or theft loss in which the official report and the claim statement conflict on a material point such as whether the premises were secured or whether the insured was present.
- An insured, a runner, or a provider has already been the subject of a confirmed SIU finding on another Northline file, and the current file shares a material feature with that finding. The mere fact that someone had a prior honest claim is not this indicator.
- A lawyer, medical provider, or body shop is on the current SIU watch list issued to claim staff. The watch list is used only for referrals. It is not announced to customers and it is not a reason to deny a claim by itself.
- An employee believes they are being asked to participate in a false claim, including by another employee or an agent.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: A large claim, a claim from a new policyholder, a claim shortly after inception, or a claim with a public adjuster is not, by itself, a referral indicator. Those facts may explain why the adjuster looks carefully at the ordinary proof. They do not, alone, go to SIU. Sending every early-tenure claim to SIU is a practice defect and will be reversed on audit.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

topic: 5.3 What the adjuster may still do
section: 5.3 What the adjuster may still do
text: Until SIU or a manager says otherwise, the adjuster continues the investigation under CLM-003, keeps the reserve honest under CLM-004, and pays undisputed unrelated amounts under CLM-005. The adjuster does not delay a make-safe vendor because a referral is open. The adjuster does not tell a vendor, an agent, or a neighbor that SIU is involved.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: The referral is the NCF form. It contains the claim number, the specific indicator, the documents that show it, what the customer has already been asked, and what the customer said. It does not contain a recommended denial and it does not contain jokes or character comments. The adjuster selects "payment hold requested" only when paying the disputed portion now would make recovery unrealistic, and a supervisor confirms the hold the same day. Holds are reviewed by SIU within two business days. A hold that SIU does not confirm is released.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: If the system is unavailable, the adjuster emails the SIU intake box with the same content and copies the supervisor. Personal email accounts are not used.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: SIU acknowledges the referral within two business days and either accepts it, declines it with a reason, or asks for one missing document. A declined referral is returned to ordinary handling. The adjuster does not re-refer the same fact unless a new indicator appears. Repeat referrals of a declined point are themselves reviewed by the claim manager and the Head of Special Investigation.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: SIU investigates the referred concern. It does not reopen every part of the customer's life. Inquiries are tied to the claim: the occurrence, the property, the injury, the other insurance, and the statements made in the claim. SIU may ask the adjuster to obtain documents through the ordinary policy duties. SIU may take an examination under oath only when CLM-003's predicates are met and a claim manager concurs. SIU may not invent a different predicate.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Surveillance, if used at all, is approved by the Head of Special Investigation and, if the claim is in suit, by the litigation supervisor. It is limited to activity that the injury or disability claim has put in issue. It is stopped when the question is answered. Reports describe what was observed. They do not diagnose the person. Adjusters are not shown raw surveillance as entertainment, and surveillance is not discussed with anyone who does not need it to evaluate the claim.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: SIU may interview the customer with the same notice rules as any recorded statement. SIU identifies itself honestly. It does not pose as a vendor, a neighbor, or a regulator. If the customer is represented, contact goes through the representative. If the customer asks whether they are being investigated, the answer is truthful at the level Legal has approved for that stage of the file: usually that Northline is reviewing a specific inconsistency, which is then described. Staff do not say "no" when the answer is yes.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: SIU completes the first assessment within fifteen business days of accepting a referral on a standard file, and within five business days if a payment hold is in place. The assessment states whether the concern is unsupported, still open, or supported. An open concern has a written plan and a predicted end date. A hold is not allowed to run past thirty days without the Head of Special Investigation's approval and a letter to the customer, approved by a claim manager, that explains the specific information still needed. The letter does not accuse. A silent hold is a service failure and, on a first-party file, a regulatory concern.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: SIU writes one of four findings:
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text:
| Finding | Meaning | What happens next |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsupported | The indicator was resolved or was never material. | Hold released the same day. Ordinary handling. The referral is not mentioned in customer letters. |
| Mistake | The fact was wrong and the customer corrected it or the records show an error without an intent to mislead. | The claim is adjusted to the true facts. No fraud language. |
| Valuation dispute | The parties disagree about price or cause, and the disagreement is not a false statement of fact. | Returned to the desk for CLM-004 and, if needed, CLM-009. Not a fraud denial. |
| Supported material misrepresentation | SIU states the false fact, the evidence, why it is material, and why the evidence shows the customer knew it was false or was reckless in the way the governing law requires. | A claim manager and Coverage Counsel decide the remedy under Section 9. |
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: SIU does not send the denial letter. SIU does not negotiate the settlement. SIU does not threaten criminal action to obtain a lower settlement. A finding is not softened or hardened because of the size of the loss or the identity of the agent.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: The remedy follows the policy and the law, not the anger the file provokes.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text:
- If the misrepresentation affects only a part of the amount, and the policy and the law allow severance, the false portion is removed and the rest is paid. The letter is a partial denial under CLM-006 and uses fraud language only with Legal's approval.
- If the policy's concealment clause and the governing law defeat the entire claim, a full denial may be approved. The letter states the facts and the clause. It is approved under the fraud-denial row of CLM-006.
- Criminal referral is a separate decision under Section 10. It is not required in order to deny, and a denial is not required in order to refer. They are not used as leverage against each other.
- Restitution for money already paid is requested in writing. Payment plans may be accepted by a claim manager. A confession of judgment or a sweeping release of unrelated rights is not demanded as the price of closing an SIU file.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: A customer who disagrees with the finding uses the appeal path in the denial letter and CLM-009. SIU does not run its own appeal. The second reviewer has access to the SIU file and is not bound by it if the evidence does not support the finding.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Northline reports suspected insurance fraud to the appropriate state fraud bureau or law-enforcement agency when the law requires a report, and it may report when the law permits a report and Legal agrees the evidence meets the Company's reporting standard. The standard is a supported finding of deliberate material misrepresentation, not a mere referral. Reports are factual, include the documents Legal specifies, and are sent by SIU leadership. Copies are kept in a restricted file. The customer is not threatened with a report to induce a settlement. If a report has been made and the customer asks, Legal decides what may be said.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Civil recovery against a third party who participated in a false claim — a shop, a provider, or an organizer — is Legal's decision. Claim staff do not invoice those parties on their own. Any recovery is coded so it does not distort the claim reserve.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Employees who are contacted by law enforcement about a claim tell SIU and Legal the same day and do not give informal statements about the file. They may acknowledge that they handled the claim. They do not speculate.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: A body shop, mitigation company, medical provider, or public adjuster whose bills appear systematically unrelated to the damage or the injury may be referred once, with examples from more than a single line item on a single file. SIU and Legal decide whether the issue is a claim dispute, a vendor-audit matter, or a reportable fraud matter. Until that decision, the vendor remains subject to ordinary estimate review under CLM-004. Staff do not blacklist a vendor in conversation, and they do not tell a customer which shops to avoid beyond the approved-network rules. Removal of a vendor from an approved network is a Vendor Management decision with a written reason.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: SIU notes are stored in the restricted section of NCF. Adjusters see the finding and the instructions that affect payment. They do not see investigative work product that Legal has marked restricted, except as needed for a denial letter's factual basis, which must be supportable from documents the letter relies on. A denial cannot rest on a secret file the customer can never test. If a fact is too sensitive to state, it is not used as a basis for the denial until Legal finds a lawful way to rely on it.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: Access to the restricted section is logged. Browsing SIU files without an assignment is a conduct violation. Retention follows the Records Schedule. A legal hold stops destruction. Closing the claim does not authorize deletion of the SIU record ahead of the schedule.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

topic: 13. Quality, training, and protections for staff
section: 13. Quality, training, and protections for staff
text: Quality Review and SIU audit a sample of referrals each quarter. They look for referrals based on protected characteristics or on mere suspicion, for indicators that were not referred, for holds that ran in silence, and for denial letters that outran the finding. Results go to the Claims Governance Committee. A desk with almost no referrals and a desk that refers a large share of its files are both examined. Either pattern can be a problem.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

topic: 13. Quality, training, and protections for staff
section: 13. Quality, training, and protections for staff
text: New adjusters complete the referral module before they handle files alone. The module uses examples of resolved inconsistencies that should not be referred and examples of documents that must be referred. SIU staff complete legal training on interviews, holds, and reporting before they accept files. Annual refreshers are mandatory.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

topic: 13. Quality, training, and protections for staff
section: 13. Quality, training, and protections for staff
text: Retaliation against an employee who refers a concern, including a concern about another employee or an agent, is prohibited. So is pressure to withdraw a referral. An employee who believes they were punished for a good-faith referral reports it to Compliance. The referral itself does not need to have been correct, only made in good faith on facts.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: There is no exception that allows an adjuster to accuse a customer of fraud in a letter because a manager is unavailable. There is no exception that allows a silent payment hold beyond the times in Section 7.3. A CAT bulletin may extend SIU's first-assessment time if volume makes the standard impossible, and it must say so in writing. It may not extend a payment hold without the customer letter Section 7.3 requires. Immediate danger — a person altering a scene while on the phone, a threat — is handled by stopping the contact and calling a supervisor and, if needed, law enforcement for the threat. That call is about safety, not about fraud reporting.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: CLM-001 and CLM-003 govern statements and documents. CLM-002 governs the concealment condition as a coverage term once SIU has a finding. CLM-004 keeps reserves accurate while a referral is open; a referral is not a reason to drop a reserve to zero or to inflate it. CLM-005 governs payment of undisputed amounts and recovery of overpayments. CLM-006 governs the denial letter. CLM-008 is not used to "recover" from an insured by calling ordinary salvage subrogation. CLM-009 is the customer's appeal. CLM-010 may adjust SIU timing in a catastrophe and does not change the definition of material misrepresentation.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text:
| Version | Date | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.0 | 1 June 2022 | Established SIU referral as a written, acknowledged process. |
| 3.1 | 1 September 2024 | Added the vendor watch-list limit after a list was misused as a denial list. |
| 4.0 | 15 November 2026 | Required a plain question before referral on a single inconsistency; banned pretext and demeanor-based referrals; set hold deadlines and customer letters; separated mistake, valuation dispute, and supported misrepresentation; prohibited using a criminal report as settlement leverage. |
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Mileage difference.** The application shows 41,000 miles and the shop writes 62,000. The adjuster asks the customer. The customer says they bought the car used, the application mileage was an estimate the agent typed, and they can send the purchase papers. The papers match 60,000 miles at purchase. This is an application-accuracy issue for Underwriting, not a claim-fraud referral, unless the customer changed the story after being shown the papers. The claim is handled on the true mileage. Underwriting is notified through the ordinary path.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

topic: Inventory item that was not there
text: **Inventory item that was not there.** After a theft, the insured lists a camera. A photo from a prior claim three months earlier shows the same camera already described as destroyed and paid. The adjuster asks, once, in plain language. The insured says it was a different camera and then cannot describe either. The adjuster refers with both photos. The adjuster does not write "insured is a fraud." SIU examines materiality and knowledge. The rest of the inventory is still evaluated. Amounts that are not in question are not held without a confirmed hold.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Early claim that is real.** A policy is thirty days old. A kitchen pipe breaks. The plumber's report, photos, and water pattern match a sudden break. The adjuster handles the claim under CLM-002 and CLM-004. A referral that says only "new policy" is declined and is recorded as an improper referral for coaching, not as a mark against the customer.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Dates in medical records.** A claimant says the collision was 2 May. The first treatment note is dated 2 April and describes the same collision. The adjuster checks for a typographical error with the provider's billing office through the ordinary authorization. The provider confirms the April date is correct and the claimant then says they "must have mixed up the month" while the wage form still claims the May date. The adjuster refers. The referral includes the confirmation. It does not include a comment on the claimant's character.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Hold too quiet.** SIU accepts a referral and the supervisor confirms a hold on the disputed jewelry portion of a homeowners claim. Twenty days pass with no letter. The dwelling payment, which is unrelated and undisputed, was correctly issued. The jewelry hold is now a problem. SIU and the claim manager send the Section 7.3 letter the same day they discover the silence, or they release the hold if the concern cannot be stated specifically enough to write the letter honestly.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Valuation, not fraud.** A public adjuster prices a roof at $48,000. Northline's measured estimate is $27,000. The difference is unit cost and a matching line. There is no false statement of what is on the roof. This is a valuation dispute under CLM-004 and, if needed, appraisal under CLM-009. An SIU referral that says "public adjuster is inflated" without a false fact is declined.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text: **Employee pressure.** An agent tells an adjuster to "keep this one off SIU, the insured is a friend of the office." The adjuster refers if an indicator is present and reports the agent's request to Agency Management and Compliance the same day. The agent's request is the conduct issue. It is not an indicator against the insured by itself.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

text:
- [ ] The indicator is a fact, and the fact is described specifically.
- [ ] A single inconsistency was the subject of one plain question first, unless asking would risk the loss of evidence or someone's safety.
- [ ] The customer's answer is in the referral.
- [ ] No comment relies on appearance, neighborhood, language, or demeanor as an indicator.
- [ ] A payment hold was requested only for the disputed portion and is confirmed by a supervisor.
- [ ] Make-safe and unrelated undisputed payments are still proceeding.
- [ ] The customer has not been told they are "being investigated for fraud."
- [ ] The referral went through NCF or the SIU intake box, not a personal inbox.
- [ ] Agents and vendors have not been told that SIU is involved.
- [ ] If a prior SIU finding is the indicator, the shared feature is named. A prior honest claim is not cited.
title: CLM-007 — Fraud, Special Investigation, and Misrepresentation

section: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery
text:
| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Document number | CLM-008 |
| Title | Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery |
| Owner | Head of Recovery, reporting to the Chief Claims Officer |
| Approved by | Claims Governance Committee |
| Effective date | 15 November 2026 |
| Next review | 15 November 2027 |
| Version | 4.0 |
| Classification | Internal — Claims and Recovery staff |
| Applies to | All lines listed in CLM-001 where the policy or the law gives Northline a recovery right |
| Supersedes | CLM-008 version 3.0 (1 June 2022) |
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: When Northline pays a loss that someone else caused, or takes title to damaged property that still has value, the Company tries to recover what it reasonably can. This policy governs that effort. Recovery is part of the claim, not an afterthought that begins the day the file closes. It is also not a second claim against the Company's own customer. Subrogation against a third party, salvage of insured property, and contribution from another insurer are different tools. Staff name the tool they are using and follow its rules.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Customers are entitled to know when a recovery will affect them. A deductible may be returned if the recovery is large enough. A release given to a responsible party may destroy Northline's rights if it is signed too broadly. This policy tells adjusters how to protect both the customer's interest and the Company's, and how to stop a pursuit that costs more than it can return.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Recovery handles subrogation, contribution between insurers, salvage, and statutory liens the Company is allowed to assert. It does not handle premium collection, ordinary overpayment letters under CLM-005, or restitution for fraud under CLM-007, except that money received is coded correctly whichever unit pursued it. Defense of Northline's insured is not compromised to improve a subrogation case. If those goals conflict, the insured's defense comes first and the conflict is documented by a claim manager.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Independent adjusters note recovery opportunities in the file. They do not send demand letters to third parties in Northline's name unless the assignment letter says they are appointed to do so.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Subrogation.** The Company's right, after payment, to pursue the person who caused the loss, standing in the insured's place to the extent of the payment. It includes contractual subrogation under the policy and equitable subrogation where the law provides it.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Made whole.** The rule, in states that apply it, that the insured is entitled to be fully compensated for the loss, including the deductible in the manner the state requires, before the Company keeps a recovery. The state addendum states which rule applies. Adjusters do not assume the Company is always first.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Salvage.** The remaining value of insured property after a total loss or a replacement, which the policy may transfer to the Company when it pays the loss. Salvage is not subrogation. The buyer of salvage is not the person who caused the loss.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Contribution.** A claim against another insurer that covers the same loss, based on the other-insurance clauses or on equitable contribution. It is not a claim against the other insurer's policyholder personally, except as that policy responds.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Waiver.** A written or, in some states, implied surrender of a recovery right. A waiver is given only under Section 8. Casual remarks are not waivers, but they can become evidence in a waiver fight, so casual remarks about "not pursuing this" are not made to adverse parties.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Recovery threshold.** The minimum expected net recovery that justifies pursuit. The current threshold is $1,000 of expected net recovery after collection cost, unless a smaller pursuit is required to return a customer's deductible and the cost of that limited pursuit is low.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text:
1. Identify the opportunity while the evidence exists, not after the debris is gone and the witnesses have forgotten.
2. Do not release a responsible party, and do not let the insured release one, until Recovery has seen the release or a manager has approved the wording.
3. The customer's deductible is not forgotten in the distribution. The addendum's made-whole or pro-rata rule is applied in the file with the arithmetic shown.
4. Pursuit stops when the expected net recovery falls below the threshold, when liability is too weak to explain to a court, or when the cost to the insured's defense is too high. Pride is not a reason to continue.
5. Collection conduct is lawful and professional. Recovery staff do not threaten criminal action, do not contact a debtor's employer except as the law allows for a judgment, and do not misstate the amount owed.
6. Salvage buyers are arm's-length. Employees and their households do not buy Northline salvage.
7. Money in is applied to the right claim, coverage part, and deductible. Unapplied recoveries are a finance defect.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: The assigned adjuster completes the recovery screen on every paid file before closure, and earlier if evidence will be lost. The screen answers:
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery
CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: A "none" answer is acceptable when it is true. A blank screen is not. Fires with a responsible contractor, water losses caused by a third party's work, product failures, auto accidents caused by another driver, and premises losses caused by a tenant's negligence are typical opportunities. Ordinary wear on the insured's own pipe is not a subrogation opportunity against the insured, and it is not an opportunity against the plumber who merely responded to the leak unless the plumber caused the damage.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Waiver-of-subrogation endorsements are read before any demand goes out. If the named insured waived recovery against a landlord or a contractor in the contract the endorsement was meant to support, Recovery closes that target and notes the waiver. Demanding anyway because the other party "can afford it" is a violation of the contract Northline issued.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Parts, vehicles, and failed products that may support recovery are held under CLM-003 until Recovery releases them or photographs and tests them. A total-loss vehicle is not sold for salvage the day the customer settles if a subrogation inspection is still needed, unless a manager approves the sale because the liability evidence is already complete. The hold is dated. Property is not stored forever. If no expert inspection is scheduled within thirty days of the hold, Recovery either inspects, releases, or obtains a manager's extension.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: When another insurer may owe contribution or may insure the responsible party, Recovery or the examiner sends a written tender as soon as the facts support it. The tender includes the claim number, the facts, the amount paid or reserved, and a request for the other carrier's position. Northline continues to meet its own duties while waiting. A tender is not a bill. The amount is updated when the payment is final.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: On product and contractor claims, a notice is sent to the potential defendant and, if known, to its insurer, asking that evidence be preserved. The notice is factual. It does not announce a lawsuit that has not been approved.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

topic: 6.3 Releases the insured wants to sign
section: 6.3 Releases the insured wants to sign
text: If an insured is asked to sign a release by a responsible party — a neighbor, a contractor, another driver — before Northline has paid, the adjuster reviews the release or sends it to Recovery the same day. The insured is advised, in writing, not to sign a release that waives Northline's rights until the wording is approved, and is told that signing may affect their claim if the policy requires them to protect those rights. The advice is not legal advice to the third party. If the insured signs despite the warning, the file documents prejudice under CLM-002 only to the extent the recovery was actually lost and the law allows that consequence. The claim is not denied automatically because a release was signed.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

topic: 6.3 Releases the insured wants to sign
section: 6.3 Releases the insured wants to sign
text: A release Northline gives a third party on a liability claim under CLM-005 is checked so it does not accidentally release a subrogation claim against a different party, and so it does not release Northline's own insured from cooperation duties that still matter.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: A demand states the facts, the legal theory in plain language, the amount paid, the deductible treatment, and the documents enclosed. It gives a reasonable response date, usually twenty-one days. It is sent to the party and to any known insurer. Demands above $50,000, and any demand that will be followed by suit, are approved by the Recovery manager. Demands above $150,000, and any demand that alleges a novel theory, are approved by Legal before they are sent.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: The amount demanded is the amount the law allows Northline to recover. Inflating a demand to create bargaining room beyond a good-faith figure is not permitted. A later reduction based on new facts is ordinary negotiation. A reduction because the first number was never supportable is a defect.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Recovery may settle within its authority table. The current limits are $15,000 for a Recovery specialist, $50,000 for a Recovery supervisor, and $150,000 for the Head of Recovery. Above that, a claim manager and Legal concur. Settlements are documented with a release that names the claim, the amount, and the parties, and that does not admit Northline's insured was at fault unless that admission is the Company's position and the insured has been consulted as CLM-005 requires.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Suit is filed only when Legal agrees the liability theory is supportable, the collection prospect justifies the cost, and the venue is proper. The statute of limitations is diaried at the start of the pursuit, not in the month it expires. A missed limitation is reported to the Head of Recovery the day it is discovered, with the amount lost. It is not quietly closed.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Pursuit is closed without recovery when:
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery
CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: The closure note states the reason and the amount abandoned. Abandoned amounts are not written off in a batch at year-end with no file-level reason.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Every recovery is distributed according to the state addendum. The file shows the gross recovery, collection costs allowed by the addendum, the insured's share, the deductible returned, and the Company's share. In a made-whole state, the insured's uninsured loss, including the deductible if the addendum includes it, is addressed before the Company retains money. In a pro-rata state, the split follows the addendum's formula. Staff do not keep the entire recovery and invite the insured to ask for the deductible later. The deductible refund, if due, is issued within fifteen business days of the recovery posting.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: If the insured has a lawyer pursuing the same defendant for amounts Northline did not pay, Recovery coordinates so the defendant is not subjected to inconsistent demands and so the insured's recovery is not undercut. Cost sharing with the insured's lawyer follows the addendum and any written agreement Legal approves. Northline does not refuse to cooperate with the insured's lawyer to improve the Company's percentage.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Money that belongs to the insured is not used to offset a premium balance unless the insured agrees in writing or the law allows the offset and Billing has confirmed it. The default is a check or electronic payment to the insured for the insured's share.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: On a total-loss vehicle, title is transferred as the state motor-vehicle rules and the addendum require, after the customer has been paid or the payment has been tendered according to CLM-005. Northline does not withhold an agreed total-loss payment to force a faster title. On real or personal property, the policy's abandonment and salvage clause is followed. The Company does not take salvage it does not want. If the Company declines salvage, the customer is told in writing that they may keep the property and the payment is reduced only if the policy and the valuation method call for a deduction. The deduction is explained in dollars.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Salvage is sold through approved salvage vendors or auctions. The sale record shows the property, the buyer, the gross price, and the fees. Employees, agents, and their households may not purchase. A vendor that handles the salvage may not buy it except through a blind auction the vendor does not run. Proceeds are applied to the claim under the reserve method in CLM-004. Until the sale, the expected salvage is reserved only as that policy allows.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Owner-retained salvage is allowed when the addendum permits and the customer accepts a documented credit. The credit is based on the salvage vendor's figure or another supportable market figure, not on a number chosen to close the file faster. Unsafe salvage — contaminated food, structurally dangerous items sold for habitable use, vehicles that should be branded — is handled as the law requires and is not sold into a use that hides the brand or the hazard.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Storage charges are reviewed monthly on open salvage. A vehicle or machine sitting in paid storage after the inspection hold has expired is a recovery failure. The Head of Recovery receives a report of salvage in storage more than forty-five days.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Contribution files are pursued on the policy language, not on a custom of "splitting it." The other carrier receives the tender, the forms relied on, and the payment proofs. If both policies claim to be excess, CLM-002's counsel path is used before anyone agrees to a split that the forms do not support. Agreements to share defense or indemnity are in writing. A phone agreement is confirmed by email the same day and is not treated as final until the writing exists.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Northline answers incoming contribution demands with the same care. A demand against Northline is logged as a claim event under CLM-001 if it alleges Northline's policy owes a payment, even if Northline already has a file. Ignoring an incoming tender because "we already closed our insured's claim" can forfeit a defense. The examiner responds within the time the tender states, or within fifteen business days if it states none.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Where Northline is a signatory to an inter-company arbitration agreement that covers the dispute, Recovery uses that forum instead of suit if the agreement requires it. Filings meet the forum's evidence rules. Awards are paid or pursued as the award states. Staff do not refuse to honor an adverse award because they disagree with it. They may seek whatever review the forum allows, with Legal's approval, and they diary the review deadline.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: A customer is not forced into that inter-company forum for their own uninsured loss. The forum decides disputes between members. The customer's deductible distribution still follows Section 8 after the award.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: A recovery reserve, or an expected-recovery code if the bulletin uses a code instead of a negative reserve, is posted when payment is made and the opportunity is more likely than not. It is not posted at intake on a hope. It is revised when liability or collectibility changes. Received funds are identified to the claim within five business days of receipt. Unidentified funds are escalated to Claim Accounting the day they are noticed. A recovery is not left in a suspense account because the file is closed. Closed files are reopened under CLM-001 to receive the money and to refund a deductible.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Charge-off of an expected recovery is approved at the same authority level that would settle it. The reason is one of the stop reasons in Section 7.3.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Recovery staff state who they are and whom they represent. They do not imply they are a regulator, a lawyer for the debtor, or a credit bureau. They do not contact a represented party directly. They accept reasonable installment plans when the amount and the person's circumstances make a lump sum unrealistic, and they confirm the plan in writing. Harassment — repeated calls after a written cease request that still leaves a lawful channel open, calls to a workplace that the law protects, or threats the Company cannot carry out — is a violation. A debtor's complaint is handled under CLM-009 even though the person is not Northline's insured.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: Quality Review samples recovery screens on closed paid files and samples demands above $10,000. A file fails if a clear third-party cause was ignored, if a waiver endorsement was overlooked, if a deductible due back to the insured was kept, if salvage was sold to a prohibited buyer, or if a limitation date was missed. The Head of Recovery reports recovered dollars, abandoned dollars, and missed limitations to the Claims Governance Committee each quarter. The report is not a quota. Staff are not rewarded for demands that are later withdrawn as unsupported.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: New Recovery staff do not send demands until they have completed the subrogation module and the made-whole module for the states they will handle. Adjusters complete a shorter module on the recovery screen and on releases. Annual training covers one waiver-endorsement example and one deductible-distribution example.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: A CAT bulletin may delay salvage pickup and may authorize a simplified recovery screen for the first thirty days. It may not waive limitation diaries or waiver-endorsement checks. There is no exception that lets an employee buy salvage. There is no exception that lets Recovery direct an insured's liability defense.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: CLM-001 creates the event number used to link clash recoveries. CLM-002 identifies other insurance and waiver endorsements. CLM-003 preserves the physical evidence. CLM-004 states when expected salvage is netted. CLM-005 governs the insured's payment, which usually happens before recovery and is not reduced by a speculative future recovery. CLM-006 is not the path for telling a third party it owes subrogation; a demand is. CLM-007 handles fraud restitution separately. CLM-009 handles disputes about distribution. CLM-010 coordinates mass salvage after a catastrophe so storage and auctions are arranged before the loss is paid, when the bulletin says so.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text:
| Version | Date | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3.0 | 1 June 2022 | Consolidated subrogation and salvage into Recovery. |
| 4.0 | 15 November 2026 | Required a recovery screen before closure; set pursuit and suit authority; required deductible distribution to be calculated in the file; banned employee salvage purchases; separated contribution from subrogation; added incoming-tender response times. |
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Contractor-caused water loss.** A roofer leaves a deck uncovered and rain damages the insured's ceiling. Northline pays the ceiling under the homeowners policy. The recovery screen names the roofer, attaches the contract and photos, and confirms there is no waiver-of-subrogation endorsement. Recovery sends a preservation notice and, after payment, a demand for the amount paid plus the deductible treatment the addendum requires. The insured is not told to sue the roofer instead of using their policy.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Waiver endorsement.** The same facts, except the policy carries a waiver of subrogation in favor of parties the insured agreed to waive in a written construction contract, and the contract with the roofer contains that waiver. Recovery closes the roofer as a target and notes the endorsement and the contract. No demand goes out. The insured's claim is unaffected.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Deductible arithmetic.** Northline paid $9,000 and the insured absorbed a $1,000 deductible. The state is a made-whole state under the addendum, and the insured has no uninsured loss other than the deductible. Recovery obtains $7,000. Collection cost allowed by the addendum is $350. The net is distributed so the deductible is addressed under the addendum's made-whole rule before Northline treats the remainder as its own. The arithmetic is in the file and the insured's check, if one is due, goes out within fifteen business days. A note that says "company keeps $7,000, insured already had a deductible" is wrong in that state.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

topic: Do not hold the customer's check
text: **Do not hold the customer's check.** The auto evaluation is agreed. Subrogation against the other driver looks likely but has not been collected. The customer's collision payment is issued under CLM-005. It is not reduced by the expected recovery. When recovery arrives, the deductible is refunded if the distribution requires it.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Salvage timing.** A total-loss vehicle is also needed for a liability photo inspection because fault is disputed and the other carrier has asked to see it. Recovery holds the vehicle, tells the salvage vendor the hold will be no more than thirty days, completes the inspection, and then releases the vehicle. The customer's payment is not delayed for the hold. Title transfer follows the payment under the addendum.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Incoming tender ignored.** Northline closed its insured's first-party file. Two months later the other driver's insurer tenders a liability claim against Northline's insured. The closer's instinct is to say the file is closed. That is wrong. The tender is logged and answered under Section 10. The liability question is investigated. The first-party closure did not decide the third-party claim.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text: **Below the threshold.** A third party scuffed a fence. Northline's payment above the deductible was $640. Collection cost would exceed the recovery. There is no product issue and no insurer to tender to. Recovery closes the opportunity under the threshold and still refunds nothing because nothing was collected. The screen explains the closure. The adjuster does not send a threatening letter "on principle."
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text:
- [ ] Possible third parties are named, or "none" is explained.
- [ ] Waiver-of-subrogation endorsements and relevant contracts were checked before any demand.
- [ ] Evidence holds are in place or deliberately released.
- [ ] Another insurer has been tendered, or ruled out.
- [ ] The statute of limitations is diaried if a claim will be pursued.
- [ ] The demand amount matches what was paid and what the law allows.
- [ ] Authority for the demand or suit is documented.
- [ ] Distribution math, including the deductible, is ready before money arrives.
- [ ] Salvage is either declined in writing, sold through an approved channel, or owner-retained with a supported credit.
- [ ] No employee, agent, or household member is the buyer.
- [ ] Incoming tenders have a response date.
- [ ] Closure of a pursuit uses a Section 7.3 reason.
- [ ] Funds are applied to the claim and are not sitting in suspense.
title: CLM-008 — Subrogation, Salvage, and Third-Party Recovery

text:
