title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: People disagree with claim decisions. This policy tells Northline how to receive that disagreement, who looks at it again, and which disputes belong in appraisal, mediation, an external review, or court. A complaint is information. It may show a wrong decision, a right decision explained badly, or a delay that would bother any reasonable person. The Company's job is to sort those cases quickly, correct what is wrong, and explain what is not, without making the customer pay for the correction in extra months of silence.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: This policy also protects the record. Regulator complaints, attorney threats, and internal appeals are logged in one place so the same customer is not given three different answers by three desks. Nothing in this policy prevents a customer from contacting a department of insurance, a lawyer, or a court. Staff never say or imply that a complaint to a regulator is disloyal, prohibited, or a reason to close a file.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: This policy covers internal appeals of claim decisions, verbal and written complaints about claim handling, department-of-insurance and attorney-general complaints, appraisal under a property policy, mediation, and the handoff of a dispute into litigation. It covers insureds, additional insureds, mortgagees to the extent of their interest, and third-party claimants. It does not cover employee grievances or agent-appointment disputes, which have their own procedures, except that a claim complaint that also alleges agent misconduct is copied to Agency Management the day it arrives.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: A question about status — "when will you inspect?" — is handled as a service contact under CLM-001 unless the customer says they are complaining or the contact alleges a broken promise, a missed payment, or unfair treatment. Staff do not force a routine question into the complaint system to inflate responsiveness numbers, and they do not keep a real complaint in the ordinary diary to avoid the system.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Complaint.** Any written communication, and any oral communication the customer asks to be recorded as a complaint, that alleges a claim was delayed, denied, underpaid, mishandled, or treated unfairly. A regulator's inquiry is a complaint even if the customer never used the word.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Appeal.** A request that a denial, partial denial, or valuation be reviewed by someone who did not make the original decision.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Appraisal.** The policy process in which each side chooses an appraiser, the appraisers or a selected umpire set the amount of a covered loss, and coverage questions stay with the Company and, if necessary, a court. Appraisal decides price and scope of a covered loss. It does not decide whether the loss is covered, unless the governing law in the addendum says a particular issue is appraisable.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Adverse decision.** A denial, partial denial, or payment the customer disputes. An offer the customer has not answered is not yet an adverse decision.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **External complaint.** A complaint forwarded by a department of insurance, an attorney general, a legislator's office, or a similar public office.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text:
1. Log first, then answer. A complaint that lives only in an adjuster's mailbox is a lost complaint.
2. The reviewer is not the person who made the decision under review, if an appeal or a regulator complaint challenges that decision.
3. Correcting a mistake is done in full, including interest the addendum requires, and is described as a correction. It is not dressed up as a compromise that implies the customer was partly wrong.
4. If the decision stands, the explanation addresses the customer's actual points. A form letter that could have been sent without reading the complaint is a failed response.
5. Deadlines from regulators are kept. If a true extension is needed, it is requested before the deadline, with a reason.
6. Customers may be represented. Once representation on the dispute is known, substantive responses go to the representative and, unless directed otherwise, to the customer.
7. Retaliation is forbidden. A complaint does not slow a payment that is otherwise due, does not affect whether a loss is covered, and is not mentioned to Underwriting as a character fact. Underwriting may see the claim outcome through the ordinary claims-history process.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Customer Relations maintains the complaint log in NCF. Any employee who receives a complaint enters it the same business day or forwards it to Customer Relations within four business hours with the claim number, the customer's words, and the channel. Branch staff do not answer a written complaint with an informal email and then skip the log. The log entry contains:
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution
CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Oral complaints are read back to the customer in summary so the log matches what they meant. If the customer says they do not want a complaint opened after hearing the summary, and the issue is only a status question, the contact may be handled as service. If the customer alleged a violation, the log stays open even if the customer later says they do not want to "make trouble." Northline still corrects a real error.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Anonymous complaints are logged and investigated to the extent the facts allow. They are not discarded because a name is missing. They are also not used, alone, as proof against an employee or a customer.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: A customer may appeal a denial, a partial denial, a depreciation or pricing decision, a deductible application, a delay that has already occurred, or a payee decision. The appeal is filed within the time stated in the decision letter. The Company standard, where the addendum is silent, is sixty days from the letter for an internal appeal. Late appeals are still reviewed if new facts are offered or if the lateness is short and explained. A very late appeal with no new facts may be closed with a letter that also reminds the customer of any external option still open. That closure is itself logged.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: The appeal goes to a reviewer who did not approve the original decision and who has authority at least equal to that approver. Coverage appeals that cited a counsel-review issue under CLM-002 are reviewed with Coverage Counsel, who was not the only author of the first opinion if that can be arranged, and if it cannot, a second lawyer in the coverage group reads the file. Value appeals may be resolved by a senior estimator's reinspection or by appraisal if Section 8 applies and the customer chooses it.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: The original adjuster supplies the file and a factual chronology within three business days. The adjuster does not draft the appeal decision. The adjuster may be asked questions. Coaching the reviewer toward a result is prohibited.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: The appeal decision is sent within fifteen business days after the file and any new customer documents are complete. If the review needs a reinspection or an expert, the customer is told the date that step will happen and the decision follows within ten business days after the step is done. The decision letter states whether the original result is affirmed, modified, or reversed, answers the customer's points, and explains any payment or interest. A reversal is paid under CLM-005 within five business days of the decision letter. An affirmation tells the customer what external routes remain, including the department of insurance and appraisal if it exists on the policy.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

topic: 7. Complaints that are not formal appeals
section: 7. Complaints that are not formal appeals
text: Service complaints — missed calls, rude conduct, a letter that could not be understood — are resolved by Customer Relations with the desk supervisor. The remedy may be an apology, a new contact, a rewritten explanation, or a correction of a handling error. An apology is not an admission that coverage exists. A coverage reversal is not hidden inside an apology. If the service review reveals that the decision was wrong, the file is moved to the appeal path and the authority in Section 6 applies.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

topic: 7. Complaints that are not formal appeals
section: 7. Complaints that are not formal appeals
text: Conduct complaints about discrimination, harassment, or a violation of the recording and privacy rules are sent to Compliance the day they are logged. The claim decision, if one is pending, is moved to a different adjuster until Compliance says otherwise. The customer is told that the conduct concern is being reviewed separately and that the claim itself remains active.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

topic: 8.1 When it is offered or accepted
section: 8.1 When it is offered or accepted
text: If the policy contains an appraisal condition and the dispute is about the amount of a covered loss, the adjuster explains appraisal in plain language when the disagreement has survived one reinspection or one documented attempt to reconcile line items. The explanation covers the customer's right to hire an appraiser, the usual requirement that each side pay its own appraiser, the umpire process, and the fact that appraisal will not decide coverage. Northline does not refuse a timely appraisal demand that the policy makes available. Northline does not demand appraisal to delay payment of items that are not disputed. Those items are paid under CLM-005.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

topic: 8.1 When it is offered or accepted
section: 8.1 When it is offered or accepted
text: If coverage is partly in dispute, appraisal may proceed on the covered portion if the policy and the addendum allow, and the coverage dispute stays on the CLM-002 path. The letter says which issues are in appraisal and which are not, so the award cannot be misread as a coverage decision.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: The appraiser is independent of the original estimator in the sense that they remeasure the disputed items. They may be a staff senior estimator who did not write the first estimate or an outside appraiser from the approved list. Northline does not appoint an appraiser who has been told what number to reach. The appointment letter tells the appraiser to determine the amount of loss under the policy. Communications with the appraiser about the merits are limited and are saved to the file. Ex parte attempts to influence an umpire are prohibited.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: When an award is issued, a claim manager reviews it within five business days for completeness and for any indication that it decided a coverage issue it was not given. If the award is valid, it is paid within ten business days, less any amounts already paid and less the deductible if not already applied. If the manager believes the award exceeded its authority, Legal is consulted before any refusal. A refusal to pay an award is a decision under CLM-006's approval levels for a denial of that amount, and it is a serious step. Disagreement with the number, by itself, is not a reason to refuse. The customer's copy of the award is sent with the payment explanation.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Northline participates in mediation when a state program requires it, when a court orders it, or when a claim manager and Legal agree it is a sensible way to resolve a specific file. The mediator is neutral. The Company representative who attends has authority to settle within a range approved before the session, or has immediate telephone access to someone who does. Attending mediation with no authority and no access is a waste of the customer's time and is not done.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Statements made in mediation are not quoted later in a denial letter as admissions, except to the extent a signed agreement incorporates them. Staff who attend are prepared on the facts and are courteous. They do not use mediation to discover the customer's finances for an unrelated purpose.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Voluntary settlement conferences follow the same authority rule. A customer is never told that refusing mediation will cause a denial or a slower payment.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: When a department of insurance or a similar office sends a complaint, Customer Relations logs it the day it arrives and assigns one owner. The owner gathers the claim chronology, the policy provisions, and the letters already sent. The response is drafted in the tone of a complete answer: what happened, in dates; what was paid or denied; what the policy says; what Northline will do next. The response does not attack the customer. It does not omit a document that hurts the Company's position if the question calls for it. Legal reviews responses that allege bad faith, discrimination, or a pattern, and any response on a file reserved above $100,000 or already in suit.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: The response goes out before the regulator's deadline. If the deadline cannot be met because a necessary document is outside the Company, an extension is requested early, and the customer-facing work continues in parallel. A copy of the response is mailed or portaled to the customer unless the regulator directs otherwise.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: After the response, the underlying claim is still handled. "We answered the department" is not a closure reason. Any commitment made in the response — a reinspection, a payment, a call by a certain date — is diaried and kept. Missing a commitment made to a regulator is reported to Compliance the day it is missed.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

topic: 10.2 Lawyers who are not yet in litigation
section: 10.2 Lawyers who are not yet in litigation
text: A letter from a lawyer that disputes a decision is an appeal or a complaint under this policy, and it is also checked under CLM-001 for whether it is a representation letter or a suit. If it is a suit, litigation intake takes over the defense response and Customer Relations still logs the complaint themes so systemic issues are counted. Direct contact with the represented customer stops, as CLM-003 requires. The lawyer receives the appeal decision within the Section 6 time unless a suit deadline makes a different response necessary, in which case defense counsel coordinates the content so the Company does not take inconsistent positions.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

topic: 10.2 Lawyers who are not yet in litigation
section: 10.2 Lawyers who are not yet in litigation
text: Threats of a bad-faith suit do not, by themselves, change the claim result. They do require the file to be reviewed promptly by a supervisor for the handling errors listed in CLM-006's extra-contractual section. If those errors exist, they are corrected. If they do not, the decision stands and the tone of the response stays factual. Staff do not write "we do not get bad faith here."
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: When a summons arrives, CLM-001's litigation path controls the deadline to answer. This policy adds the dispute-resolution duties around that event. Customer Relations flags any open complaint on the same claim so defense counsel knows what has been promised. Counsel receives the claim file, the complaint log, and a privilege instruction. The adjuster remains responsible for reserves under CLM-004 and for settlement authority under CLM-005 unless the litigation supervisor reassigns those duties in writing.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Employees do not speak to opposing counsel about the merits except through defense counsel. Employees who receive a call from a reporter about a lawsuit refer the call to Communications and do not comment. A customer who sues may still receive claim payments the policy owes. Suit is not a reason to freeze an undisputed amount.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Settlement of litigation follows CLM-005 and counsel's recommendation. The claim manager records why the settlement differs from the pre-suit evaluation if it does. A difference is allowed when discovery changed the facts. A difference that exists only because the Company wants the suit to go away, with no factual change and above the evaluation range, requires the next authority level and a note that says so plainly.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: The complaint log, appeal letters, appraisal awards, mediation agreements, and regulator responses are part of the claim file and follow the Records Schedule. They are not stored only on a Customer Relations drive that claim staff cannot see. Personal data in a complaint is handled under the privacy rules. A complaint from one claimant is not placed in another claimant's file except as a cross-reference that does not reveal medical or settlement details.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Customers may request copies of the letters they were sent and of their own submissions. Requests for the entire internal file, including reserve notes and legal advice, are routed to Legal. Front-line staff do not email the claim file to satisfy a caller who cites a statute they cannot identify. Legal answers within the time the privacy addendum requires and withholds only what the law allows to be withheld. If Legal withholds a document, the response says a category was withheld and why, in the form the addendum requires.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Customer Relations reports monthly to the Claims Governance Committee: complaint counts by cause, average days to respond, reversals, commitments missed, and regulator files past deadline. A rising cause — for example, holdback explanations or mortgagee payees — is sent to the owner of the underlying policy so the upstream document can be fixed. Treating the monthly report as a public-relations exercise while the upstream policy stays broken is itself a governance failure.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: Quality Review reads a sample of appeal affirmances to see whether the customer's points were answered, and a sample of reversals to see whether the original error is being coached. Repeat errors by the same person after coaching go to the desk manager. Repeat errors of the same type across a desk go to a policy or template fix.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: All claim staff complete the complaint module: how to log, what not to say, and how appraisal differs from coverage. Customer Relations staff complete regulator-response training before they sign a department response. Annual training includes one redacted file in which a complaint was justified and one in which it was not, so staff see that both outcomes are normal.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: There is no exception that allows a regulator deadline to be missed without an approved extension. There is no exception that allows the original decision-maker to decide their own appeal. During a catastrophe, CLM-010 may add Customer Relations staff and may publish a temporary address for complaints. It may not close the appeal right or lengthen a statutory response time. A customer who files the same complaint repeatedly without new facts receives one consolidated response and a statement of how further duplicates will be acknowledged. Duplicates are still logged. They are not investigated from scratch each time if nothing has changed and the prior response is still accurate.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: CLM-001 receives lawsuits and representation letters. CLM-002 and CLM-006 are the decisions most often appealed. CLM-003 supplies reinspections. CLM-004 and CLM-005 supply the numbers and the payments a reversal requires. CLM-007 findings may be appealed through the denial letter; SIU does not run a separate appeal. CLM-008 recovery disputes by third parties are logged under this policy. CLM-010 may increase complaint volume and does not change the review standard.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Appeal of a pipe denial.** The customer appeals a partial denial of a supply line, enclosing a plumber's letter that the line was damaged by a sudden freeze rather than wear. The original senior adjuster does not decide the appeal. The reviewer reads the screen, the photos, and the new letter, and may ask an engineer one written question. The decision addresses the freeze theory specifically. If the new evidence is better, the decision reverses that item, pays it, and calculates interest. The reviewer's letter does not say "as previously explained" without the explanation.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Rude call, right decision.** The customer complains that an adjuster hung up and that the deductible is wrong. Customer Relations confirms the deductible arithmetic, which was correct, and confirms from the recording that the call was ended abruptly. The response apologizes for the call, states the deductible math, and does not pretend the deductible changed because the call went badly. The adjuster is coached on the hang-up separately. The coaching is not described to the customer in disciplinary detail.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Appraisal scope.** The roof price is disputed. The cause of interior stains is not agreed. Northline pays nothing for the roof while demanding appraisal of the whole house, including items the customer did not dispute. That is a violation. The undisputed items are paid. Appraisal is offered or accepted only on the disputed amount of the covered roof. The interior stays in investigation until cause is decided. The letter draws that line.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Regulator deadline.** A department complaint arrives with a fourteen-day response date. The file is large. Customer Relations assigns an owner the same day, sends a holding call to the customer, and drafts the chronology. If a key inspection note is missing, the owner finds it or says in the response that it cannot be located and what Northline will do. The owner does not wait until day fourteen to discover the note is missing. Any promise in the response is diaried before the response is sent.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Suit and an open complaint.** The customer complained about a delayed rental car and then sued for bodily injury. Defense counsel is told about the rental issue and the promise, already made, to pay two more weeks of rental. The promise is kept. It is not withdrawn because a suit was filed. The injury claim is defended on its facts. The complaint log stays visible on the file.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text: **Duplicate complaints.** The customer sends the same portal message weekly. The first message was answered in full and nothing has changed. Customer Relations logs each message, sends a short acknowledgment pointing to the prior answer, and does not open a new investigation each week. If the fourth message adds a new fact, that fact is reviewed.
title: CLM-009 — Appeals, Complaints, and Dispute Resolution

text:
- [ ] The complaint is in the log the day it was received.
- [ ] The reviewer did not make the original decision, if the decision is what is challenged.
- [ ] Regulator deadlines and promised actions are diaried.
- [ ] The response answers the points the customer actually raised.
- [ ] A reversal is paid as a correction, with required interest, within five business days of the decision.
- [ ] An affirmation states the remaining external options.
- [ ] Appraisal, if used, is limited to amount-of-loss issues the policy allows.

- [ ] A represented customer's lawyer is included on the response.
- [ ] Conduct allegations went to Compliance.
- [ ] No language discourages a regulator complaint.
- [ ] Commitments in the response match diaries on the claim.
- [ ] The original adjuster was not allowed to draft the appeal result.
- [ ] Suit papers, if any, have been sent to litigation intake the day they arrived.

title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: A catastrophe is a surge of claims from one event, large enough that ordinary staffing, ordinary inspection timing, and ordinary vendor capacity will not carry it. A large loss is a single claim whose size, injuries, or complexity would overwhelm a standard desk even if it happened alone. This policy tells Northline how to declare those situations, how authority and timelines change while they last, and which rules do not change at all. The coverage test in CLM-002, the evidence rules in CLM-003, the reserve honesty rules in CLM-004, the payee rules in CLM-005, the denial rules in CLM-006, and the complaint rules in CLM-009 remain in force. A catastrophe is not a suspension of the contract the customer bought.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The operational goal is simple to say and hard to do: people who cannot live in their homes or operate their businesses get a fast, accurate response, and the Company does not pay the wrong cause of loss because the queue is long. Speed is planned in advance so it does not depend on heroics the week the storm arrives.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: This policy applies when the Chief Claims Officer or a designated deputy declares a catastrophe event, and when any file meets the large-loss definition whether or not a catastrophe is open. It binds employees, independent adjusters appointed for the event, and firms on the catastrophe vendor panel. It does not, by itself, change reinsurance treaties. Reinsurance notices required by those treaties are still made, using the facts this policy's reporting section produces.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: A busy Friday, a local hail cell with forty claims, or a single commercial fire below the large-loss threshold is handled with ordinary tools plus a supervisor's workload plan. Those events are not given a catastrophe code to avoid ordinary timelines. Mis-coding is a reporting violation because it pollutes the Company's catastrophe data and the customer's deductible treatment if a percentage deductible is wrongly triggered.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Catastrophe event (CAT).** A declared event with a CAT code, a named peril, a geography, a start time, and an expected end of new losses. The code is what attaches a claim to the event. A claim is not a CAT claim because the customer used the word "storm."
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **CAT bulletin.** The written instruction issued for that event. It is the only place ordinary timelines, desk-adjustment permission, advance amounts, and price-list deviations may be changed. Verbal instructions in a briefing are confirmed in the bulletin the same day or they expire.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Large loss.** A file with an indemnity reserve of $250,000 or more, a fatality, a suit seeking extra-contractual damages, a commercial loss that stops a business above the reserve threshold, or any file the large-loss unit accepts because of complexity. The threshold matches the reinsurance notice line in CLM-004 so the two systems do not diverge.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Desk adjustment.** A decision based on photos, aerial imagery, invoices, and statements, without a visit, allowed only when the bulletin or CLM-003 permits it and the photo standard is met.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Make-safe.** Temporary work to protect property from further damage: tarping, board-up, water extraction, temporary power or fencing when needed for safety. It is not the permanent repair.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Advance.** A payment of a stated amount before the full estimate, credited to the final payment, allowed only as the bulletin or CLM-005 describes.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Deployed adjuster.** A staff or independent adjuster assigned outside their home territory for the event, working under the bulletin and a Northline examiner.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text:
1. Declare early, in writing, with a code and a map. An undeclared emergency produces undeclared exceptions.
2. The bulletin may relax a Company timeline. It may not relax a statute, a payment duty on an undisputed amount, or a safety duty.
3. Cause of loss is still required. Wind, flood, storm surge, and wear are not lumped into one payable pile because the neighborhood was hit hard.
4. Customers hear from a person who has the file. Mass emails do not replace the acknowledgment and status duties except as the bulletin expressly allows and the law permits.
5. Vendors are on the panel or are approved for the event in writing. A truck that arrives uninvited is not given a Northline assignment because it is convenient.
6. Large-loss files get a named examiner and a second set of eyes. They are not left in the CAT queue because the event is busy.
7. When the event is over, the code is closed, the exceptions expire, and files return to ordinary handling. Exceptions do not linger out of habit.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The Chief Claims Officer declares a CAT after notice from weather services, claim-volume monitoring, or civil authorities that a peril will produce, or is producing, losses beyond ordinary capacity. A deputy designated in writing may declare if the Chief Claims Officer is unreachable, and the Chief Claims Officer confirms or ends the declaration within twenty-four hours. The declaration names the peril, the states or counties, the start time, the CAT code, and the initial desk that will run operations.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: A declaration is not a statement that every loss in the area is covered. Communications staff are told that distinction before any public message goes out. Public messages tell customers how to report, how to perform make-safe work, and how to reach Northline. They do not say "if you had damage, you are covered."

text: Each bulletin version is numbered. Staff follow the current version. Old versions stay in the event file so a later audit can see what rule was in force on a given day.

text: The Chief Claims Officer closes the CAT code when new notices have returned to a volume the ordinary desks can take and the fieldwork backlog is assigned. Closure is written. After closure, new claims from the same storm are still coded to the event if the date of loss falls inside the event window, but they use ordinary timelines unless the bulletin's tail section says otherwise. The tail section has an end date. Open files do not keep CAT exceptions indefinitely.

text: The First Notice Desk uses the CAT script from CLM-001. The minimum data set still applies. In addition, the opener records whether the dwelling is habitable, whether anyone is injured, whether a tree or power line is creating danger, and whether the customer needs the make-safe advance. Duplicate searches are not skipped. A second claim for the same house and the same storm is a supplement or a duplicate, not a new event, unless a second policy is involved.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: If phone lines are saturated, the bulletin may direct customers to the portal and may staff an overflow vendor whose scripts Northline has approved. The vendor opens files in NCF or in a bridge system that is loaded into NCF the same night. A spreadsheet that is not loaded is not a claim file. The acknowledgment still goes out within the bulletin's time, with a claim number, a contact path, and make-safe instructions. Customers are told to keep receipts and to photograph damage before temporary repairs if they can do so safely.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Agents in the affected area may be unable to forward notices the same day. The bulletin may give agents a short, stated extension and must still treat notice to the agent as notice to the Company under CLM-001. Customers are not charged with the agent's outage.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The operations lead assigns geography, licenses, and lodging before adjusters travel. An adjuster who is not licensed where the state requires a license does not inspect there. Deployed staff receive the bulletin, the price list, the photo standard, and a safety briefing. They do not begin inspections until that briefing is done. Daily check-in is mandatory. An adjuster who misses check-in is contacted. If they cannot be reached and a safety concern exists, the operations lead escalates to local emergency contacts. Production targets are secondary to the safety briefing's rules on roofs, standing water, curfews, and heat.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The inspection note meets CLM-003. In a catastrophe the note also records flood line or water height if water is alleged, wind direction indicators the adjuster actually sees, roof covering and age if known, and whether damage is clearly older than the event. "Storm damage throughout" is not a note. Where the bulletin allows desk adjustment, the photo set must show each elevation, the roof if safely photographed by the customer or a drone vendor, interior stains with a wide shot that locates them, and a photo of the front of the risk for identification. If the photos are not enough to separate causes, a visit is scheduled. Desk adjustment is a permission, not a quota.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: If the home is not safely habitable for a covered cause, the adjuster authorizes additional living expense within the policy and within their authority the day of the inspection, or the day the photos prove it on a desk file. The customer is told the time limit and the dollar limit in writing, in the same week, not after the first hotel bill is rejected. Advances for short-term lodging follow the bulletin. Evacuation orders alone do not create additional living expense if the policy requires a covered loss to the dwelling. The letter says so plainly when that is the decision, and a denial of living expense is still a denial under CLM-006.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Wind, hail, flood, storm surge, sewer backup, and tree fall can happen in one weekend and damage one house. The adjuster separates them. The screen cites the facts for each. Flood and storm surge are not paid under a homeowners policy that excludes them because a CAT was declared. A flood policy, if Northline writes one on the same property, is a second claim number under the same event, handled on that form. Wind damage above a flood line can be covered while damage below it is not. The estimate is split. A single estimate that calls everything "hurricane" and pays it all is a defect. A single estimate that denies everything "because of flooding" without looking at the wind damage above the line is also a defect.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Percentage wind or named-storm deductibles are applied only when the declarations and the event meet the form's definition. The bulletin may remind staff of the definition. It may not create a deductible the policy does not have, and it may not waive one the policy does have, except where a regulator's binding order requires a waiver and Compliance confirms the order in the bulletin. The arithmetic is shown on each file, as CLM-002 requires.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Matching, ordinance or law, and ensuing-loss questions are decided under CLM-002. CAT volume does not create a shortcut denial and does not create a shortcut payment of code items that were not triggered.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The panel is chosen before storm season and confirmed in the bulletin. Fees, documentation standards, and the rule against assignment of benefits, if the policy prohibits it, are in the vendor contract. A vendor that solicits Northline customers with a promise that the deductible will be waived or that the roof will be "covered by insurance" is reported to Vendor Management the day staff learn of it. Northline does not waive a deductible to match a contractor's promise. Staff warn the customer, plainly, that the deductible is the customer's share and that a contractor who offers to hide it is asking them to participate in a false invoice. That warning is given without accusing the customer of already agreeing.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Price-list increases are allowed only under the bulletin, with a reason and an end date. An adjuster who meets a genuinely higher local price writes the variance on the estimate. A general "CAT factor" typed into every file is not allowed. Supplements are audited. After the event, Vendor Management samples invoices against photos. Systematic overbilling is referred under CLM-007's vendor section and is pursued as a vendor-audit recovery. It is not ignored because the vendor was helpful in the first week.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Off-panel firms are used only when the panel cannot reach a geography and a manager approves the firm in writing for a stated period. The firm receives the bulletin's documentation rules before the first assignment. Firms that will not document to that standard are not hired.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The large-loss unit reviews every file that crosses the threshold the day it crosses, and every fatality the day it is reported. A CAT file that is also a large loss is dual-tracked: the CAT code remains for event reporting, and the large-loss examiner owns the strategy, the reserve, and the coverage screen. The file is not left with a deployed independent adjuster as the final decision maker.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Within three business days of acceptance, the examiner writes a plan: cause experts, counsel if a suit or a coverage question requires it, a reserve path, a customer-communication owner, and a reinsurance notice. The plan identifies what could move the number by a material amount. On a commercial property loss that stops operations, the plan includes business-interruption documents, a mitigation conversation with the insured, and a diary for the extra-expense and period-of-restoration issues. The insured is given one primary contact. They are not asked to repeat the loss story to a new person each week unless the contact changes for a stated reason, in which case the new contact reads the file first.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: A fatality or a serious bodily-injury CAT claim is referred to the casualty large-loss examiner even if the property damage is small. Contact with the family is respectful, limited to what the claim requires, and coordinated with counsel if liability is in question. Staff do not request an examination under oath of a grieving family as an early step. Reserves follow CLM-004, including a realistic severity based on the facts then known, not a token. Communications about the event go through Communications. The examiner does not speak to the press.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

topic: 11. Payments, complaints, and recovery in the surge
section: 11. Payments, complaints, and recovery in the surge
text: Advances authorized by the bulletin are paid to the correct payees under CLM-005, credited on the final estimate, and not described as a final settlement. Undisputed portions of a split wind-and-flood loss are paid when the wind portion is measured. They are not held until every coverage question on the property is closed, unless the open question could erase the wind payment itself and that possibility is documented.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

topic: 11. Payments, complaints, and recovery in the surge
section: 11. Payments, complaints, and recovery in the surge
text: Complaint volume rises after a CAT. CLM-009 stays in force. The bulletin may add Customer Relations staff and publish a temporary contact. It may not authorize a script that tells people their appeal will have to wait until next season. Regulatory deadlines are kept.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

topic: 11. Payments, complaints, and recovery in the surge
section: 11. Payments, complaints, and recovery in the surge
text: Recovery and salvage under CLM-008 are organized for the event: a salvage staging plan, a hold on vehicles and equipment needed for subrogation, and a clash list of losses caused by one contractor or one product. The event number is the key. Individual files still receive their own recovery screen before closure. A CAT is not a reason to skip subrogation against a contractor whose work failed in the storm, and it is not a reason to pursue neighbors who were equally victims of the weather.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The bulletin names a Communications owner. Customer-facing messages are approved by that owner and by Claims for accuracy. Messages include how to file, what make-safe work is reimbursable if the loss is covered, what photos help, and a warning about uninvited contractors and deductible-waiver schemes. Messages do not estimate how fast every roof will be repaired and do not promise coverage.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Internal rumors are corrected in the next bulletin. Adjusters do not tell customers "everyone is getting a new roof" or "nothing is being paid until the governor announces something." If a governmental order changes a duty, Compliance writes the effect into the bulletin and staff quote that, not a headline.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Customers who cannot return home, who have lost phones, or who are in shelters are given flexible contact methods. A letter sent only to a destroyed house does not count as notice if the file shows the house is uninhabitable and another channel exists. The adjuster records the channel that worked.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Finance and Claims reconcile CAT payments weekly during the event: advances outstanding, indemnity by peril, expense, and vendor accruals. The reconciliation is an internal control. It is not a target that adjusters are told to hit. Reserves on CAT files follow CLM-004. A simplified intake reserve may be used for seventy-two hours if the bulletin says so. After inspection, the evaluated reserve replaces it. Large-loss and treaty notices go out under CLM-004 the day a threshold is crossed. Reinsurance reporting uses the CAT code so a clash is visible. Adjusters do not call reinsurers.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: After closure of the code, the Reserve Committee reviews development on the event at ninety days and again at the next quarterly reserve study. Persistent under-reserving at first inspection is corrected in the method, as CLM-004 describes, not by a speech about leakage.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Deployed staff are told the maximum consecutive workdays in the bulletin. The operations lead sends people home or to rest when the limit is reached or when fatigue makes field work unsafe. Production numbers are not a reason to extend the limit. Alcohol during the workday, inspections conducted under the influence, and harassment of customers, residents, or coworkers are grounds for immediate removal from the event and for disciplinary action. Local curfews and exclusion zones are obeyed. An adjuster turned away by emergency management does not sneak into a neighborhood to finish a roof count.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Customers in crisis are spoken to with patience. A person who has lost a home may be angry or disorganized. That is not an indicator under CLM-007. A false invoice scheme is an indicator. The difference is the facts, and staff are trained on it before deployment.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

topic: 15. Quality during and after the event
section: 15. Quality during and after the event
text: During the event, Quality Review samples desk adjustments, split cause-of-loss estimates, advances, and habitability decisions in near real time, not only after the code closes. A failed desk adjustment — photos that do not support the cause, or a flood item paid as wind — is corrected on that file and the estimator is coached before they write the next ten estimates. After the event, a larger sample is scored for deductible accuracy, mortgagee payees, unsupported line items, and timelines. Results are reported to the Claims Governance Committee with the event's complaint and reopening rates. Independent adjusters with poor scores are not reappointed to the next event until they are retrained. Firms with systematic overbilling are removed from the panel.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

topic: 15. Quality during and after the event
section: 15. Quality during and after the event
text: Employees are not punished for a slow week caused by access restrictions, and they are not rewarded for estimate totals. The score is accuracy, safety, and kept promises.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Before the season, Claims runs a readiness review: panel contracts current, licenses mapped to likely states, bulletin template updated, intake scripts loaded, lodging process tested, and the large-loss on-call list confirmed. Gaps are assigned owners and dates. A readiness review that produces no changes in a year when the prior event's audit found defects is not a serious review.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: Staff who will deploy complete the CAT module: split causes, deductible types, desk-photo standards, advances, and safety. Independent firms complete it before they receive a code. A firm that shows up without the module is not assigned files. Annual training uses one redacted mixed wind-and-flood file and one commercial interruption file so large-loss examiners and CAT adjusters have seen the same facts from both procedures.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: The only operational exceptions to ordinary claim rules during a catastrophe are the ones written in the current bulletin and allowed by Section 5.2. A field briefing does not add exceptions. A large-loss file may receive more resources than this policy requires. It may not receive fewer controls. If NCF fails during an event, the outage procedure in CLM-001 applies, the operations lead assigns a paper-control owner, and the backlog is keyed in priority order: uninhabitable dwellings, injuries, and then other claims. Payments already promised are reconciled first so duplicate checks do not go out when the system returns.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: CLM-001's catastrophe intake section is the front door. CLM-002 is the coverage test the bulletin cannot rewrite. CLM-003 is the inspection standard, including preservation of evidence. CLM-004 is the reserve method and the large-loss notice line. CLM-005 is how advances and final payments are made. CLM-006 is how any denial, including a living-expense or flood denial, is issued. CLM-007 is the referral path for invoice schemes and is not the path for ordinary storm claims. CLM-008 is salvage, clash, and contractor recovery. CLM-009 is the complaint path during and after the surge.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Declaration.** A hurricane is forecast to cross two states where Northline writes homeowners and commercial property. The Chief Claims Officer declares the event the day before landfall, assigns a code, and issues a bulletin that allows a $2,500 make-safe advance, sets a photo standard for desk adjustment of minor exterior losses, and names the tarp panel. The public message tells customers how to board up and how to file. It does not say all hurricane damage is covered. Claims inside the geography with a different date of loss are not given the code.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Split causes.** A house has a water line four feet up the wall and missing shingles on the south slope. The policy excludes flood and covers wind. The estimate pays the wind-damaged roof and the interior damage that the facts show came from rain through the wind opening. It does not pay the lower four feet of drywall if the facts show flood. The letter itemizes both decisions. A one-line denial of the entire claim "due to flooding" is returned by quality review. A one-line payment of the entire contractor invoice is also returned.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

topic: Desk adjustment refused by the facts
text: **Desk adjustment refused by the facts.** The customer uploads a photo of a wet ceiling and a distant shot of the roof. The bulletin allows desk adjustment only when elevations and the roof are shown well enough to separate wind from wear. The adjuster schedules a visit or a drone inspection. The file is not paid as wind, and it is not denied as wear, on the weak photo set.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Advance and mortgagee.** The bulletin allows a $2,500 make-safe advance. The dwelling has a mortgagee. Under CLM-005 and this bulletin, an advance of that size for temporary tarping may be paid to the insured or the approved tarp vendor with the insured's direction, and the bulletin says which. A permanent roof payment of $18,000 still names the mortgagee. The advance is credited. The customer is not told the advance was "extra."
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Contractor at the curb.** A contractor tells the insured the deductible will be "taken care of" if the insured signs an assignment. The adjuster tells the insured the deductible will be applied, that Northline pays from its own estimate, and that a false deductible waiver on an invoice is not something the Company will honor. The contractor is reported to Vendor Management. The insured is not referred to SIU because a contractor made an offer. A referral happens if a false invoice is actually submitted and the insured adopts it after a plain question, under CLM-007.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Large loss inside a CAT.** A cold-storage facility loses its roof and its inventory in the same hurricane. The reserve crosses $250,000 the first day. The large-loss unit takes the file that day, assigns one contact, hires a cause-and-origin expert and an accountant under CLM-003, notices Reinsurance, and leaves the CAT code in place for aggregation. The deployed roof adjuster may measure the roof. The deployed adjuster does not settle the inventory or the business interruption.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **Fatigue.** An adjuster has worked the bulletin's maximum days and says they can "do one more street." The operations lead says no and reassigns the street. The decision is not a performance mark against the adjuster. An adjuster who continues after being stood down is removed from the deployment.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

text: **End of exceptions.** The code is closed on 1 October. A supplement on a coded claim arrives on 20 October. The tail section ended on 15 October. The supplement is handled on the original claim under ordinary CLM-003 and CLM-004 timelines. The adjuster does not apply the expired desk-adjustment shortcut. A new hail loss on 20 October is a new claim and is not given the hurricane code.
title: CLM-010 — Catastrophe and Large-Loss Claims

- [ ] Any change to acknowledgment or inspection time cites the legal limit it stays inside.
- [ ] Desk adjustment, if allowed, names the photo standard and the size band.
- [ ] Advances, if allowed, name the amount, the payee rule, and the credit to the final estimate.
- [ ] Price-list changes have a reason and an end date.

- [ ] Deductible treatment is a reminder of the forms, not a new deductible.

- [ ] Reinsurance notice is assigned to a named role.
- [ ] The tail, or the lack of a tail, has an end date.
- [ ] Communications has approved customer-facing language, and that language does not promise coverage.
